# Objective

Make the worklog-selection-list plugin's chord shortcuts **extensible per project**: the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` provides the default chords, and a **project-local `shortcuts.json`** (discovered from the resolved worklog root) provides additional entries and overrides. Today `loadShortcutConfig()` reads only the bundled file, so projects cannot add project-specific chords without forking the plugin.

## Problem statement

A consuming project (open_source_llm) needs a `w` chord that dispatches `/skill:wiki-podcast-script --doc <path> --force-single` / `--rewrite <path>` to a pi agent pane for podcast episode work items. That chord is project-specific and must **not** be added to the core plugin's bundled `shortcuts.json` (operator decision). The plugin currently loads shortcuts exclusively from `join(__dirname, 'shortcuts.json')` (see `loadShortcutConfig()` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts`), so there is no supported way to add or override chords per project.

## Users

Herdr users of the worklog-selection-list plugin, and projects that consume it (e.g. open_source_llm's podcast production workflow).

- As a plugin user, I want the plugin's built-in chords (c, n, p, i, r, s, …) to remain available by default, so I can keep the standard workflow unchanged.
- As a project maintainer, I want to add project-specific chords (e.g. `w` → write podcast script) in a local file without editing the plugin source, so upgrades/rebuilds of the plugin do not lose my chords.
- As a project maintainer, I want a local chord with the same key sequence as a bundled one to override the bundled behavior, so I can tailor defaults per project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadShortcutConfig()` loads the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` as before (backward compatible; no local file → identical behavior to today).
- [ ] When a project-local `shortcuts.json` exists, its entries are merged: new chords are added, and a local entry whose chord sequence (+ view) matches a bundled entry overrides it (local wins). Override semantics are documented and unit-tested.
- [ ] The project-local file is resolved relative to the **worklog root** (the root that `configureWorklogTarget()` / `resolveWorklogRoot()` resolves from `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, i.e. the directory containing `.worklog/`), so the same plugin install serves different chords in different projects.
- [ ] Local file location and merge order are documented in the plugin README (config section), including the override rule and validation behavior.
- [ ] Malformed local entries are logged and skipped without breaking the bundled defaults (same defensive posture as the bundled parser; invalid values never crash or hide shortcuts).
- [ ] Existing chord behavior is unchanged when no local file is present; full `npm test` suite (shortcut-config tests and others) passes.

## Design notes / open questions

- **Local file location:** proposal is `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` (next to `.worklog/`). Alternative: a hidden name (`.herdr/shortcuts.json` or `.pi/shortcuts.json`) to avoid a bare `shortcuts.json` in the project root. The worklog root already has `.worklog/`; a `shortcuts.json` next to it is simple and discoverable. Confirm which location is preferred (see Open Questions).
- **Override key:** chord sequence + view (`'list'|'detail'|'both'`) is the natural key. A local entry with the same chord+view replaces the bundled entry; same chord with a different view coexists. A local `stages` filter narrows availability (already supported by `ShortcutEntry`).
- **Merge mechanics:** `loadShortcutConfig()` currently takes no arguments. Extend it to accept the resolved worklog root (or read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`), parse both files, and merge (bundled first, local appended/overriding). The registry already de-duplicates by exact lookup; explicit override handling must be added so duplicate chords do not produce ambiguous lookups (`lookupChordEntry` uses `entries.find` — the first match wins, so local entries must replace bundled ones at the same key, not just be appended).
- **`code_freeze`:** local entries may carry `code_freeze` like bundled ones (parser already supports it); no extra work expected.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `loadShortcutConfig()` merge logic, override handling, optional local-path argument.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — new tests: no-local-file (identical defaults), local adds new chord, local overrides bundled, malformed local entry skipped, per-project resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the resolved worklog root into `loadShortcutConfig()` (note: `loadShortcutConfig()` is currently called before `configureWorklogTarget()` in `main()`; the call order or plumbing must be adjusted so the local file is found).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the local `shortcuts.json` convention, merge/override rules, and location.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — no change expected (already passes `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`); confirm.

## Related work

- Consuming work item (open_source_llm worklog): **Add 'w' chord to write podcast script in ContextHub worklist plugin (OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS)** — needs this extensibility to add its `w` chord without touching the plugin's bundled shortcuts.
- **Model selection per shortcut (WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3)** — added the `model` field to shortcut entries; the local-config extension must preserve it (parser already handles it).
- **Code-freeze shortcut visibility (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)** — added `code_freeze` to shortcut entries; preserved by the same parser.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the project-local file should live at the worklog root (or a documented sub-path there) so the plugin can find it with the already-resolved root; exact name to be confirmed.
- **Risk:** duplicate chord sequences between bundled and local files must be resolved deterministically (local wins) or `entries.find` will silently pick the bundled one. Explicit override logic + tests mitigate.
- **Risk (scope creep):** full user-level config files (per-user, per-host), hot-reload of shortcuts, and UI for editing shortcuts are out of scope; track separately if requested.
- **Compatibility:** projects with no local file must see byte-for-byte identical behavior (guard against regressions).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (eng/producer):** Local file location — `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.herdr/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.pi/shortcuts.json`? `.pi/settings.json` already exists at the project root of the consuming repo, so `.pi/` has precedent as a project-config location; `.herdr/` is more plugin-scoped. Recommend one and confirm.
- **OPEN QUESTION (eng):** Should the override key be chord+view only, or also stage? (Chord+view is the minimal key; stage is a visibility filter, not an identity.) Recommend chord+view.
data.title: Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Auto-downgrade critical priority when item is marked completed/in_review

## Problem statement

A work item that is marked **completed/in_review** can still carry `critical` priority today. Critical is a signal for urgent *open* work — it drives `wl next` ordering, TUI selection lists, and grouping — so a finished item left at critical competes with genuinely urgent items and makes dashboards misleading. When an item transitions to a terminal state (`status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`), its priority must not remain `critical`.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** who close out work items.
  - *As an operator, when I mark a critical item as completed/in_review, I want its priority automatically downgraded to `high`, so that finished work stops competing with genuinely urgent open items.*
  - *As a developer, I want the automatic downgrade reported in the command output, so that I can verify the change happened.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state — `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` (via `wl update`) or `status=completed` (via `wl close`) — its priority is automatically downgraded to `high`.
2. Priorities other than `critical` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) are never modified by a terminal transition.
3. Command output reports the downgrade: a machine-readable field in `--json` output and a summary line in human-readable output, consistent with the existing `downgradedChildren` reporting in `wl update`.
4. Unit tests cover: `wl update --status completed`, `wl update --stage in_review`, `wl close`, and no-op cases (non-critical priorities unchanged; non-terminal transitions like `plan_complete` leave `critical` intact).
5. Full project test suite passes, and `CLI.md` documentation for `wl update` / `wl close` is updated to describe the auto-downgrade behavior.

## Constraints

- Canonical priorities are `critical | high | medium | low` (see `src/validators/priority.ts`); the downgrade target is `high` per operator specification.
- Only terminal transitions trigger the downgrade — moving `critical` items between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must not touch priority.
- Must not conflict with the existing child cascade: `cascadePriorityDowngrade` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (parent downgrade → children). A completed item is itself terminal, so no child cascade is implied by this rule.
- Prefer reusing existing reporting patterns from `src/commands/update.ts` over inventing new output formats.

## Existing state

- The database allows any priority with any status/stage; there is no rule preventing `critical` on completed/in_review items today.
- Terminal transitions are: `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (`src/commands/update.ts`) and `wl close <id>` (`src/commands/close.ts` sets `status=completed`, `stage=done`).
- A directly related cascade already exists: `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (line ~1230) downgrades critical *children* to `high` when a parent drops from `critical`, reported via `downgradedChildren` in `src/commands/update.ts` (lines ~383–408).
- `wl doctor` validates status/stage combinations (`src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`) but has no priority-vs-stage rule.

## Desired change

1. Add a small helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal(updatedItem)` or an inline check alongside the existing cascade) that, when an item is transitioning to a terminal state, downgrades `critical` → `high`.
2. Invoke it from the terminal-transition paths in `src/commands/update.ts` (stage/status changes) and `src/commands/close.ts` (close path). Decide between explicit call sites vs. enforcement inside the shared `update()` — prefer explicit call sites to avoid side effects on internal cascade `update()` calls unless a guard makes it safe.
3. Report downgraded items in JSON and human-readable output, mirroring the `downgradedChildren` pattern.
4. Add unit tests and update `CLI.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling (`--status completed` / `--stage in_review`); add downgrade enforcement and reporting.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path sets `status=completed`; enforce downgrade here too.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — home of `cascadePriorityDowngrade`; natural location for the new helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal`) if a DB-layer helper is preferred.
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — canonical priority constants to reuse.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and/or `tests/cli/*`) — unit tests for the new behavior.
- `CLI.md` — document auto-downgrade in `wl update` / `wl close` sections.

## Related work

- `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)` — completed; the direct precedent: same `critical` → `high` downgrade rule and reporting pattern, but for parent→child cascades.
- `Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G)` — completed; priority validation infrastructure (`src/validators/priority.ts`).
- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — completed; critical-priority semantics in `wl next`.
- `Exclude in-review items from wl next (WL-0ML2TS8I409ALBU6)` — completed; in_review semantics.
- `Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6)` — open; sibling rule about terminal-state invariants on parents.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl doctor` detection/fix of legacy `critical` + completed/in_review items is a natural extension but is NOT part of this work item's ACs. If wanted, record as a separate linked work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9`).
- **Over-enforcement risk:** blanket enforcement inside the shared DB `update()` could interfere with internal calls (e.g., the child cascade calls `db.update()`); guard conditions must be precise or enforcement kept at explicit call sites.
- **Assumption:** "completed/in_review" means terminal transitions — `status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`, plus `stage=done` via `wl close`.
- **Assumption:** the downgrade target is `high`, as explicitly specified by the operator.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The request ended with `--priority low` — what does it refer to?
  - A (assumed, rgardler): `--priority low` sets the priority of this new work item itself (matching `wl create --priority low` CLI syntax), not the downgrade target — the feature spec explicitly downgrades to `high`. Source: interactive reply; interpretation documented here. If wrong, the item priority is a one-line `wl update` fix.
- No further clarification was needed; the seed context was sufficient to draft the brief (interview skipped per intake skill step 4).

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)

# Intake Brief: Remove OpenBrain (WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA)

## Problem statement

OpenBrain is an optional integration (`src/openbrain.ts`) that spawns the `ob` CLI to submit a summary whenever a work item is marked completed. This project enabled it for local testing (`openBrainEnabled: true` in `.worklog/config.yaml`, commit `66fb51a8`) but the `ob` binary is not installed, so every `wl update`/`wl close` that completes an item emits `[openbrain] ...` errors to stderr. The integration is unused and, per producer confirmation, is to be **removed entirely** — both from the shared codebase and from this project's config.

## Users

- **Developers** running `wl update`/`wl close` in this project — they see stray `[openbrain]` errors and want clean output.
- **Worklog maintainers** — they want dead integration code (which requires an `ob` binary nobody has and whose `wl openbrain` commands were never implemented) removed from the shared CLI.

User stories:
- As a developer in this project, I want `wl update` to complete a work item without emitting `[openbrain]` errors, so my terminal output is clean.
- As a Worklog maintainer, I want the OpenBrain integration absent from the shared codebase, so there is no dead code and no misleading docs/plugin references.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Feature removed from the shared codebase**: `src/openbrain.ts` deleted; `submitToOpenBrain` imports and call sites removed from `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/commands/close.ts`; `openBrainEnabled` removed from `WorklogConfig` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
2. **Project-scoped disablement**: `openBrainEnabled: true` removed from `.worklog/config.yaml` in this repository.
3. **No dangling references or dead artifacts**: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`, and `docs/openbrain.md` deleted; OpenBrain references removed from `CLI.md` and `README.md`. A repo-wide search (`rg -i "openbrain|submitToOpenBrain|openBrainEnabled"`) returns no matches in tracked source/docs (excluding git history and regenerated `dist/` artifacts).
4. **Error gone**: completing a work item via `wl update` and `wl close` in this project produces no `[openbrain]` stderr output (validated by the CLI test run, AC5).
5. **Green build & docs**: full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation reflects the removal (README, CLI.md, code comments, docs table).

## Constraints

- No behavior changes beyond removing the OpenBrain path — `wl close`/`wl update` semantics (recursive close, re-sort, audit handling) are untouched.
- Worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/*` are separate feature branches — do not edit them in this change; only the main checkout is in scope.
- Config user file `.worklog/config.yaml` is the only place `openBrainEnabled` is set in this repo; `config.defaults.yaml` does not set it (verify at implementation time).
- The optional retry-queue file `.worklog/openbrain-queue.jsonl` may exist from failed submissions; it is transient data, not code — no action required beyond optionally removing it.

## Existing state

- `src/openbrain.ts` implements `submitToOpenBrain()` (spawns `ob add --stdin --title …`), `buildOpenBrainSummary()`, `appendToQueue()` (retry queue), and `resolveObBinary()` (`WL_OB_BIN` or `ob`).
- `src/commands/update.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(item)` when `updates.status === 'completed'` and `config.openBrainEnabled`.
- `src/commands/close.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(updated)` from the force, audit-gated recursive, and standard close paths when `config.openBrainEnabled`; the recovery path comments reference OpenBrain.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: `WorklogConfig` declares `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- `.worklog/config.yaml`: `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- Docs: `docs/openbrain.md`; `CLI.md` lists `wl openbrain status/resubmit` (commands were never implemented); `README.md` docs table links `docs/openbrain.md`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- `ob` is not on PATH and `WL_OB_BIN` is unset; the globally installed `wl` (`/usr/local/bin/wl`) symlinks to this repo's built `dist/cli.js`, so a rebuild is required to actually stop the errors.

## Desired change

Remove the OpenBrain integration and its project config toggle:

- Delete `src/openbrain.ts`, `docs/openbrain.md`, `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- In `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/close.ts`: drop the `submitToOpenBrain` import and every `openBrainEnabled` fire-and-forget block (including the recovery-path comment).
- In `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: remove `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- In `.worklog/config.yaml`: remove `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- In `CLI.md` / `README.md`: remove OpenBrain references.
- Rebuild (`npm run build:shared && npm run build`) so the installed `wl` no longer ships `openbrain.js` in `dist/`.

## Key Files:

- `src/openbrain.ts` — delete (entire module)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — remove import + completion call block
- `src/commands/close.ts` — remove import + three close-path call blocks + recovery comment
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — remove `openBrainEnabled` from `WorklogConfig`
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — remove `openBrainEnabled: true`
- `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts` — delete
- `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts` — delete
- `docs/openbrain.md` — delete
- `docs/feature-requests/openbrain-playwright-fallback-retrieval.md` — delete (OpenBrain feature request; would fail AC3 repo-wide search)
- `CLI.md`, `README.md` — remove OpenBrain references

## Related work

- WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC — "Whenever a work item is marked as completed/done update OpenBrain": introduced the integration (predecessor).
- WL-0MOHP1FIP007LYCB — "Make wl close OpenBrain submission fully non-blocking": changed the close flow (predecessor).
- WL-0MNRPS89H004COB0 — "Fix validator and openbrain test failures": fixed CLI.md docs + EPIPE handling (predecessor).
- WL-0MRTSOK8C009CDLA — "Process lifecycle utility module": references `src/openbrain.ts` as a spawn user; the process-lifecycle/spawn helpers themselves must be preserved.
- WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9 — ruff lint fix whose description matched `docs/openbrain.md` (search-index noise only).

## Effort and Risk

- Effort: **S** — deletions plus a handful of targeted edits; rebuild required.
- Risk: **Low** — opt-in flag; no other project enables it; `ob` unavailable so no live dependents. Residual risks: missed references (mitigated by the AC3 repo-wide search) and stale built `dist/` (mitigated by the rebuild in Desired change / AC5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (Map/intake, 2026-09-19): "Should 'Remove openbrain' mean (A) remove the integration from the shared `worklog` codebase (~600 lines), or (B) only disable it in this project's `.worklog/config.yaml` (one line)? The title points at (A), the description ('in this project, but not any other … disable it') at (B). Reply A, B, or both."
  - **Answer (producer): "Both"** — do (A) **and** (B): remove the feature from the shared codebase AND remove the `openBrainEnabled: true` line from `.worklog/config.yaml`. Source: producer reply to comment WL-C0MU89PEMR004ISDS on WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA.

# Dispatch-logs Skill: Generate Global Dispatch Reports

A `/skill:dispatch-logs` command that produces a concise, human-readable (or JSON) 24-hour dispatch activity report across all projects on the machine — including leader state, timeline, errors, and coordination status — with support for custom time windows and per-project filtering.

## Problem Statement

Operators investigating overnight dispatches must manually aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files across all projects on the machine. There is no single command to produce a concise 24-hour (or custom window) global dispatch report.

## Users

- **Operator on-call**: Needs a quick view of what dispatches ran overnight and whether any errors occurred.
- **Debugging engineer**: Tracing a specific dispatch failure across projects.
- **Team lead**: Reviewing dispatch activity trends over a custom time window.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:dispatch-logs` produces a human-readable report covering all projects on the machine for the last 24 hours (default window).
2. All invocation flags work correctly: `--hours N`, `--since`/`--until` ISO timestamps, `--project <name>`, and `--json` for machine-readable output.
3. The report includes five sections: (a) leader summary, (b) dispatch timeline, (c) error summary, (d) coordination state, and (e) known issues.
4. Gracefully handles the case when no dispatch logs exist (produces an empty/clean report, not an error).
5. Unit tests pass for log parsing, argument handling, and report structure (using mocked log files).
6. SKILL.md is complete with name, description, invocation examples, and frontmatter.

## Constraints

- Log files are in JSONL format (one JSON object per line).
- Machine coordination state lives in `~/.herdr/downtime/` (two JSON files).
- Must skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` directories during project root discovery.
- Default window is 24 hours from `Date.now()`; custom windows use ISO 8601 timestamps.

## Existing State

- Per-worklog dispatch logs exist at `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Machine-wide coordination at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json`.
- Companion debug item (WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV) adds per-strike stderr/exitCode — the dispatch-logs skill should note when this data is unavailable.

## Desired Change

Create a new skill in `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/` with:
- `SKILL.md` — skill definition with frontmatter and invocation docs.
- `scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Python script implementing the report generation.
- `tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — unit tests with mocked data.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/SKILL.md` — New skill definition file.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Core logic: argument parsing, log discovery, parsing, report generation.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — Unit tests.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` — Read-only coordination state.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-leader-lease.json` — Read-only leader lease.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Resist adding extra report sections beyond the five specified (leader summary, dispatch timeline, error summary, coordination state, known issues).
- **Discovery performance**: Walking from `~` to find all project roots could be slow on machines with many repositories; consider caching or a configurable root list.
- **JSONL format consistency**: Assumes all projects write logs in the same JSONL format; malformed lines should be skipped gracefully.
- **Coordination files**: Assumes `~/.herdr/downtime/` files are present and readable; handle missing files gracefully.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV** — "Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable" (companion; provides richer per-strike data the dispatch-logs skill should report on).
- **WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE** — "Extend dispatch log schema and add pane lifecycle monitor" (may affect log parsing).
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** — "Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason" (enriches available log data).
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — "Log herdr downtime dispatches" (established the per-worklog log architecture).

# Intake Brief — Add a priority icon to the selection list (WL-0MTQYTA20009YXBT)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection list shows status, stage, producer review, and epic icons in its icon prefix, but the priority icon is only rendered as text after the title. Users scanning the list should see a priority icon alongside the other status indicators for at-a-glance prioritisation.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using the Herdr worklist to browse and triage work items.
  - User story: "As a developer scanning the Herdr worklist, I want to see a priority icon as the first icon in each row so I can quickly identify urgent items without reading the full priority text."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Herdr worklist selection list icon prefix (in `getIconPrefix` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) includes a priority icon as the first icon, before the existing agent status slot.
2. The priority icon uses the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` map from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`: critical → 🚨, high → ⭐, medium → 📋, low → 🐢.
3. The priority icon respects the existing `noIcons` option — when icons are disabled, `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` text is shown instead.
4. The `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` is increased to accommodate the additional icon (from 12 to 13 cells), and alignment is preserved.
5. The work item `priority` field is already passed through the item type accepted by `getIconPrefix`.
6. All existing tests continue to pass; new tests are added for the priority icon in the prefix (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.

## Constraints

- Must extend the existing `getIconPrefix` function in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — do not create a parallel icon system.
- Must preserve the existing `WL_NO_ICONS=1` / `noIcons` option behaviour.
- Must not break the fixed-width alignment (`ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`) — adjust the constant if needed.
- Visual-only change in the Herdr worklist rendering; no persisted data model changes.
- The priority icon must appear **first** in the icon prefix row.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**: The `getIconPrefix` function composes an icon prefix with columns: agent status (fixed-width slot), status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, and optional epic icon. The `PRIORITY_ICONS` and `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` maps exist but are not used in the prefix.
- **`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`**: Calls `getIconPrefix(item, { noIcons })` and prepends the result before the item ID/title. The `item` type already includes `priority?: string`.
- **Priority text** is already rendered after the title as `${priorityIcon(item.priority, { noIcons })} ${item.priority}` (line 1255 of worklist.ts).

## Desired change

1. **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**:
   - Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend the priority icon as the first icon in the prefix.
   - The new column layout (left to right):
     - 0. Priority icon
     - 1. Agent status (existing fixed-width slot)
     - 2. Status icon
     - 3. Stage icon (for in_review items, shows audit-aware icon instead)
     - 4. Producer review flag
     - 5. Optional epic icon
   - Update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` from 12 to 13 to account for the additional icon.
   - Update the JSDoc comment for `getIconPrefix` to document the new column layout.

2. **Tests**: Add/update tests for the priority icon in `getIconPrefix` (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).

3. **Documentation**: Update any relevant documentation (e.g., `docs/icons-design.md` if it exists).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend priority icon; update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — No changes needed (item type already includes `priority`)
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — New tests for priority icon in `getIconPrefix`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts` — Updated tests verifying priority icon in rendered prefix

## Related work

- **WL-0MQEI5DYO009736I** — "Add stage and audit result icons to TUI work item selection list" (completed) — established the pattern for adding icons to `getIconPrefix`.
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (completed) — ensured consistency between list and metadata sections.
- **packages/shared/src/icons.ts** — Core icon module; `PRIORITY_ICONS` map already defined.
- **packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts** — Worklist renderer that calls `getIconPrefix`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Adding a priority icon increases the icon prefix width from 12 to 13 cells, which may reduce available width for the item ID/title on narrow terminals. Mitigation: The existing truncation logic in `worklist.ts` already handles width overflow — it truncates lines to fit the terminal.
- **Assumption**: The `item.priority` field is always available on items displayed in the worklist. If `item.priority` is undefined/null, the priority icon function returns an empty string (handled by the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` lookup with a default empty string).
- **Assumption**: The priority icon emoji (🚨⭐📋🐢) are all single-cell wide in the terminal, matching other icons in the prefix.
- **Scope creep mitigation**: Any additional features (e.g., priority-based colouring of the entire row, priority sorting changes, priority filters in the metadata panel) should be recorded as separate linked work items rather than expanding this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the priority icon appear in the icon prefix? The current order is: agent status, status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, epic icon." — Answer: "The first icon in the row of icons in the selection list should be a priority icon." # Intake Brief — Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC)

**Headline**: Extend the now-correct Dispatcher-workspace anchor so every automated downtime dispatch lands in a per-project tab inside the Dispatcher workspace, named after the work-item prefix (e.g. `WL`, `TCE`), giving operators instant per-project separation without leaving the neutral workspace.

## Problem statement

The automated downtime dispatcher has been fixed to always spawn into a dedicated **Dispatcher** workspace regardless of which herdr instance holds the leader lease (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG / WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX, F1–F3 landed on `origin/dev`). All dispatches currently share the single root tab/pane in that workspace. With two active worklogs (ContextHub `WL-…`, Tableau Card Engine `CG-/TCE-…`, plus other roots) this collapses per-project separation — overnight runs for different projects intermix in one grid and operators must inspect each pane's `cwd`/label to tell them apart.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running 2+ project workspaces** (e.g. ContextHub, Podcast-editor, Tableau Card Engine):
  > "As an operator, I want every automated downtime pane that belongs to project prefix `TCE` to appear in a `TCE` tab of the Dispatcher workspace (and `WL` panes in a `WL` tab), so I can see per-project progress at a glance without mixing projects in one grid."

- **On-call / overnight dispatch reviewer**:
  > "As an on-call engineer reviewing morning dispatches, I want the Dispatcher workspace to contain one tab per project (labelled by the work-item prefix), so I can sweep each project's automated work independently."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-prefix tab routing inside the Dispatcher workspace** — an automated downtime dispatch for work item `<PREFIX>-<hash>` creates (if absent) or reuses a tab labelled `<PREFIX>` inside the machine-wide Dispatcher workspace and spawns its pane inside that tab. Example: `WL-0MTO…` → `WL` tab, `TCE-…` / `CG-…` → tab named exactly after the id prefix before `-` (so `TCE` items land in `TCE`, `WL` items in `WL`). Verified via `herdr tab list` (tabs filtered to `workspace_id == Dispatcher` carry `label == prefix`) and `herdr pane list` (each `Downtime triggered …` pane's `workspace_id == Dispatcher` and `tab_id` equals the prefix tab's `tab_id`, with `cwd` equal to the item's worklog root).
2. **Idempotent, concurrent-safe tab provisioning** — the first dispatch for a previously unseen prefix creates the tab exactly once; concurrent first-dispatches for the same new prefix do not create duplicate tabs with the same label in the Dispatcher workspace. Re-provisioning handles stale state: a persisted per-prefix anchor whose tab/pane is no longer alive is detected and re-created on the next dispatch for that prefix.
3. **No regression to existing dispatcher invariants** — Dispatcher-workspace anchoring (no fallback to the leader's current pane — `anchor-unavailable` still means "no dispatch this cycle"), per-item `cwd` forwarding, CAS `wl update --if-status/--if-stage` claim, staged-marker exclusion, `code-freeze` and `needsProducerReview` gates, selection/coordination/round-robin semantics, and dispatch audit logs (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) remain unchanged; pane spawn still goes through `send-to-pi.sh` / `grid.py` (now targeting the per-prefix tab's anchor pane rather than the single workspace anchor when a prefix tab exists).
4. **No leftover duplicate workspace or orphan tab state** — after the change there remains exactly one `Dispatcher` workspace (label `Dispatcher`, `w13` today) holding all per-prefix tabs; repeated dispatches for the same prefix do not leak extra tabs or panes beyond the expected grid growth; a persisted file (e.g. extended `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` or a new `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` in the machine coordination dir) tracks `{ workspaceId, byPrefix: { "<PREFIX>": { tabId, paneId } } }` under the coordination lock and is the authority for reuse.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Automated downtime dispatch only — scope is `dispatchFromCoordination` / `dispatchDowntimeWork` → `dispatchClaimedTier`; manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows keep their current-pane/tab behavior.
- Single `Dispatcher` workspace (C0) is retained — per-project separation is by **tabs** inside it, not by additional workspaces.
- Prefix extraction is the work-item id substring before the first `-` (e.g. `WL-…` → `WL`, `TCE-…` → `TCE`, `CG-…` → `CG`); tab label is exactly that prefix (case-preserved, no normalisation beyond the raw prefix).
- Tab/pane provisioning must use the existing machine coordination dir (`~/.herdr/downtime`, via `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts`) and the coordination lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock`) — no new lock mechanism; `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <PREFIX> --no-focus` (or `workspace create` + `tab create`) and `herdr pane split --pane <anchorPaneId>` / `grid.py` remain the herdr surface.
- Fail-safe: if the per-prefix tab/anchor cannot be resolved/provisioned, the dispatch degrades to `anchor-unavailable` (no dispatch this cycle), never to a leader-workspace fallback or to the wrong tab.
- Herdr CLI JSON shapes may vary across versions (`tab_id` vs `tabId`, `pane_id` vs `paneId`, nested `result`) — parsers must tolerate variants and log raw output on parse failure rather than silently producing `anchor-unavailable` every cycle.

## Existing state

- **C0 anchor-by-ID landed on `origin/dev` (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG):** `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` provisions one `Dispatcher` workspace + root pane and persists `{ paneId, workspaceId }` to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` under the coordination lock with an aliveness (`pane get`) check and stale re-provision; `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchClaimedTier` resolves `getDispatcherAnchor(cwd)` before the CAS claim and forwards `anchorId` to `spawnAgentPane` → `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` → `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py --cwd <target>` (split + rebalance around the anchor) or plain `pane split --pane <id>`.
- **Live state:** `herdr workspace list` shows one authoritative `Dispatcher` workspace `w13:t1` (pane_count 1); `herdr tab list` shows `w13:t1` label `1`; `herdr pane list` shows `w13:p2` `Downtime triggered audit …` (evidence the anchor path is working after the WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX fix).
- **Gap:** all prefixes currently share `w13:t1`; there is no `herdr tab create --label <PREFIX>` path, no per-prefix persistence, and `grid.py` / `send-to-pi.sh` have no tab-aware anchoring — a new prefix-aware resolver plus `tab create` + per-prefix anchor mapping is required.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the Dispatcher anchor module to per-prefix tabs** — replace/augment the single-anchor persistence with a map `byPrefix` (e.g. `{ workspaceId, byPrefix: { "WL": { tabId, paneId }, "TCE": { tabId, paneId } } }`) stored in the machine coordination dir; the resolver `getDispatcherTabAnchor(cwd, prefix)` (or `getDispatcherAnchor` extended to take a prefix) does: ensure the `Dispatcher` workspace exists → list tabs in that workspace (`herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) to find `label == prefix` → validate the tab's anchor pane is alive (`pane get`) → return `{ workspaceId, tabId, paneId }` or, if absent/stale, create it under the coordination lock (`herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <PREFIX> --no-focus`, capture `tab_id` + `root_pane.pane_id`), persist under lock, and return it. Double-check inside the lock before creating to avoid duplicates.

# Intake Brief — Text inputs miss keypresses when extension is syncing — pause sync while user is typing (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH)

## Problem statement

All in-extension screens that present a text input intermittently drop keypresses. The suspected cause is a background `wl sync` (and its follow-up list refresh/re-render) firing while the user is typing, contending for the TUI event loop or replacing render state mid-keystroke. There is no user value in syncing/refreshing while a form is active — it should be deferred until typing finishes.

## Users

- **Extension users typing in any form** — creators/editors filling fields in the Herdr worklist pane and any other in-extension overlay that accepts free-text input.
- **Operators triaging during incident flows** — users who rapidly fill forms while background workers run.

Example user stories:
- As a user filling the command-parameter form (`FormState` — unknown `<identifier>` prompts), I want every keystroke to register so I can submit the command without retyping.
- As a user writing a ship-it note / md note in the Ship-It dialog, I want the dialog to not lose characters when a periodic sync fires.
- As a user, I want the worklist to resume auto-sync/refresh promptly after I close the form, so I still see fresh data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Sync suppressed while typing:** While any text-input overlay is open, background `wl sync` is not spawned. Verified by running with `autoSync=true` and holding a form open for ≥2× `syncIntervalMs`: zero `wl sync` spawns (or, equivalently, the sync scheduler tick is skipped) — heartbeat/single-flight/visibility gates remain intact when not typing.
- [ ] **AC2 — Refresh/re-render suppressed while typing:** While any text-input overlay is open, auto-refresh list refetch/re-render is skipped so keypresses are not dropped. Verified by a deterministic unit/integration test that simulates rapid keystrokes into `FormState`/`ShipItDialogState` across a scheduled refresh tick — zero dropped characters; refresh resumes within one interval after the overlay closes.
- [ ] **AC3 — Coverage of all text-input screens:** The guard applies to every current text-input entry point (`form-dialog.ts` `FormState`, `ship-it-dialog.ts` `ShipItDialogState`, `md-note-edit.ts` note editing, and any other modal input) via a single shared predicate (e.g. `isTyping()` / `isInputActive()`) — not a per-screen copy-paste — so future inputs are covered by extending one place.
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression when not typing:** When no input is active, existing behaviour is unchanged: auto-refresh (30s default), auto-sync (60s default), visibility/heartbeat/DB-change gates, and downtime/mode-switch workers continue as before. Existing unit tests for `worklist.ts` / `auto-sync.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing & validation:** New unit tests cover: (a) sync tick skipped while form/ship-it dialog open; (b) refresh tick skipped while form/ship-it dialog open; (c) ticks resume after close; (d) typing simulation loses no keystrokes across ticks. A manual verification checklist is documented in a work-item comment (hold form open, observe no sync/refresh; close, observe resume).
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not regress existing gating: visibility (pause-when-hidden), single-flight, cross-instance heartbeat dedup, and DB-change skip must remain.
- Fix must be low-risk and narrowly scoped — gate the scheduler ticks, don't restructure the TUI event loop or form handling.
- Fire-and-forget sync semantics stay: skipping a tick is silent; no error surfacing while typing.
- Critical priority — dropped input is a data-loss-adjacent UX failure; prefer a minimal, reviewable patch.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` registers two periodic scheduler tasks: `refresh` (`autoRefresh`, 30s) and `sync` (`autoSync`, 60s, `fireImmediately:true`) which calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`. Both are visibility-gated (`paneGate.visible()`) but have no typing/input gate, so they fire even while `formState !== null` / `shipItDialog !== null`.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` provides `runSync` / `SyncTimer` with `ifIdle` single-flight and heartbeat dedup, but no caller-side typing guard.
- Text-input overlays: `form-dialog.ts` (`FormState.handleInput`/`render`), `ship-it-dialog.ts` (`ShipItDialogState`), `md-note-edit.ts` (note edit flow that opens a `FormState`). Keypress handling in `worklist.ts` correctly routes to `formState.handleInput` when open, but the background tick still runs concurrently.
- Related hardening exists: thrash prevention / lock-storm fixes (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E), idle-gated refresh (WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I), pause-when-hidden (WL-0MSB447GC0004CAW). None gate on typing.

## Desired change

- Introduce a single shared predicate (e.g. `isInputActive()` / `isTyping()`) that is true whenever any text-input overlay is open (`formState !== null || shipItDialog !== null || md-note-edit active || filter text input if applicable`), and check it at the top of the `refresh` and `sync` scheduler tick handlers (alongside the existing `paneGate.visible()` check) to skip `doSync`/`doRefresh` while typing. Record the decision to resume on close (next tick fires normally — no extra immediate refresh required, or document if one is desired).
- Ensure the guard also covers any other periodic background refresh that would cause a re-render/lost focus while typing (audit explicitly whether `downtimeWorker`/`modeSwitchWorker` need gating; if not, document why — they don't touch the list render path while a modal is open).
- Add unit tests for the typed-gating and a manual smoke checklist; update in-code comments and docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add typing/input gate to scheduler tasks (`refresh` and `sync` ticks) and define shared `isInputActive` predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — No direct change expected, but verify `runSync` single-flight/heartbeat semantics are preserved; add comment if gating is caller-side.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — Defines `FormState`; reference for predicate coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog.ts` — Defines `ShipItDialogState`; reference for predicate coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-note-edit.ts` — Note-edit text input flow; ensure covered.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add typing-gated scheduler tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — Regression guard (no behaviour change when not typing).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Documents the typing gate (pause background work while a form is open).
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — Typing-gate behaviour + manual smoke verification procedure.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E — wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync (completed) — prior sync thrash hardening.
- WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I / WL-0MSB445BP0057ZQT — idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget (completed) — existing gating to extend.
- WL-0MSB447GC0004CAW — Docs & verification: pause-when-hidden behavior (completed) — visibility gate sibling.
- WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF — Selection list refreshes immediately when its tab/pane regains focus (completed) — refresh cadence context.

Source: initial report "All in-extension screens that all text input will sometimes miss keypresses." No separate screen inventory was provided; brief assumes the three known overlays and a shared predicate to future-proof.
- Q: What exactly should be paused — `wl sync` only, or also list refresh / similar background work? — Answer (operator spec, WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH): "There is no need to do that (or similar) when the user is typing into a form in the extension." Interpreted as: at minimum suppress `wl sync` and the list `doRefresh` that would re-render/lose focus; audit other periodic ticks (downtime/mode-switch) and explicitly gate or document why not. Source: initial report sentence 2.
- Q: Should we debounce, buffer, or queue a refresh after typing ends? — Answer (Map, assumption — no producer input yet): Defer, don't queue: skip ticks while typing; next regular tick after close fires normally. If product wants an immediate post-close refresh, it can be added as a follow-up without changing the gating contract. Documented as assumption in Constraints/Desired change.

# Intake Brief — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations

**Headline:** Audits are incorrectly invalidated by mechanical operations (re-sort, sync merges, and other timestamp-churning writes) that bump `updatedAt` without changing the work item's substantive state. This work item fixes all three paths so that audits are only invalidated by actual acceptance-criteria-relevant changes.

## Problem statement

Audits are being invalidated by non-semantic operations (re-sort, same-timestamp merge during sync, and other writes) that bump `updatedAt` without changing the work item's substantive state. The audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats these items as "edited after audit", causing passing audits to read as stale and items to linger in open queues unnecessarily.

**Producer clarification:** Audits should only be invalidated by (a) change in acceptance criteria, or (b) change in code impacting the acceptance criteria.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not appear as "needs re-audit" after mechanical operations like re-sort or sync.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited but invalidated only by timestamp churn.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical operations.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Re-sort does not invalidate audits:** `batchUpdateSortIndices` and the single-item re-sort path no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today. Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run re-sort, assert the audit is still fresh and `updatedAt` is unchanged.

2. **Same-timestamp merge does not invalidate audits:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` in sync no longer bumps `updatedAt` when the merged result equals one side (or converges without bumping). Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` synced repeatedly converge with no unbounded timestamp advancement; existing audit freshness preserved.

3. **General protection against non-semantic `updatedAt` bumps:** Mechanical operations (re-sort, sync merges, audit persistence) do not bump `updatedAt`. Substantive edits (status change, description edit, priority change) still bump `updatedAt` as today, correctly invalidating audits. The `saveAuditResult` pattern of resetting `updatedAt = auditedAt` is preserved. Regression test: audit an item, update its `assignee` or `tags` — audit should remain fresh.

4. **Full project test suite passes** with all new regression tests.

## Constraints

- Surgical changes confined to: `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` (batchUpdateSortIndices), `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` (mergeSameTimestampItems), and `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (if needed).
- No schema changes.
- Semantic edits must still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- Backward compatible: no CLI flag changes required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`** — `batchUpdateSortIndices` runs `UPDATE ... SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed.
- **`packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423`** — `mergeSameTimestampItems` sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:1269`** — `saveAuditResult` already resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.

## Desired change

1. In `batchUpdateSortIndices`, skip updating `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`.
2. In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field; converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side.
3. Consider extending the pattern in `saveAuditResult` (reset `updatedAt` to `auditedAt`) to other operations that should not invalidate audits, or implement a broader "semantic vs non-semantic change" detection mechanism. Document the chosen approach.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems` (line ~L423)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), recency scoring (line 2215)
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — Add regression tests for both failure modes
- `tests/database.test.ts` — Add reSort ordering tests for audit freshness

## Related work

- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child)
- **WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS** — Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely (child)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Boost audit-backed items in wl next sorting (established freshness rule)
- **WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V** — Concrete victim example: audited "Ready to close: Yes" now carries stale updatedAt from re-sort (referenced in WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable audit-invalidation policies or per-field granularity. **Mitigation:** Keep this item to the three concrete scenarios; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Checking whether a change is "semantic" vs "non-semantic" could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Simple whitelist of non-semantic operations (sortIndex updates, timestamp-only sync merges) is sufficient for now.
- **Regression risk:** Other parts of the system (TUI, herdr, sync) may depend on `updatedAt` being bumped for certain operations. **Mitigation:** Review all `updatedAt` references before changing; add integration tests for TUI selection, herdr dispatch, and sync convergence.
- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** The producer's definition of "change in acceptance criteria" may need clarification during implementation (e.g., should changing `assignee` or `priority` invalidate audits?). **Assumption:** Only status, description, and priority changes are semantic; metadata changes (tags, assignee, stage, issueType) are not. Document final rule in code comments.
- **Assumption:** The two child items (WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA, WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS) remain the primary victims; their existing acceptance criteria are subsumed by this broader fix.
- **Sync conflict risk:** Preventing `updatedAt` bumps in `mergeSameTimestampItems` may affect conflict resolution if both sides have divergent content. **Mitigation:** Preserve the existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which specific audit invalidation scenarios? — Answer (producer): All three — re-sort (WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA), same-timestamp merge (WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS), and any other write. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Bug fix or new feature? — Answer (producer): Bug fix — existing invalidation mechanisms are causing incorrect behaviour. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When should audits be invalidated? — Answer (producer): Only by (a) change in acceptance criteria, or (b) change in code impacting the acceptance criteria. Source: interactive reply.

## Problem

The llama-proxy returns a specific 503 when every provider is outside its scheduled
`available_times` window:

    All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window

The recovery classifier in this repo does not match that wording:

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — `DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS`
  contains `/all providers exhausted/i` and `/no provider available/i`.
- The proxy message says "All providers **unavailable**" and "no provider **is** available",
  so neither pattern matches.
- Result: `ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN` → `register-recovery.ts` shows
  `Unrecognized error: …` and performs **no** retry.

This is the follow-up to WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK (which added the generic
`All providers exhausted` pattern).

## Change

Add patterns so the time-window exhaustion 503 is classified as `SERVER_ERROR` (retryable):

- `/all providers unavailable/i`
- `/no provider\s+(is\s+)?available/i`
- `/scheduled time window/i`
- optionally `/outside its available_times/i`

Add classification tests (see `error-classification.test.ts`). Longer term, prefer keying off a
machine-readable `code`/`type` field if the proxy adds one (tracked on the proxy side).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The exact proxy message is classified as `SERVER_ERROR`, not `UNKNOWN`.
- [ ] No regression to existing classifications (all existing tests pass).
- [ ] A test asserts the full proxy string classifies correctly.
- [ ] If/when the proxy exposes a stable `code`, classification prefers it over prose (follow-up).

# Intake Brief — wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills (WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K)

## Problem statement

The `refactor` and `standup` skills read and (for refactor) create worklog data, but neither begins by pulling remote worklog changes. A stale local SQLite store can therefore produce duplicate `REFACTOR` work items, stale standup reports, and un-pushed local changes. The requested behaviour is that **`wl sync` runs as the first action** of both skills, before any other worklog interaction.

## Users

- **Agents invoking `/skill:refactor` or `/skill:standup`** — they need current worklog data so analysis and reporting are based on the same state the operator sees.
  - *As an agent, I want refactor/standup to sync first, so I never file duplicate smells or report stale items.*
- **Operators reading standup reports** — the report must reflect the actual remote queue.
  - *As an operator, I want my standup to reflect synced data, so it drives the right priorities.*
- **Producers reviewing refactor-filed work items** — fewer duplicate `REFACTOR` items to triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:refactor` (both the no-ID full-project scan and the `<id>` session-only mode) performs `wl sync` as the **first worklog operation**, before any work-item read, comment injection, or work-item creation. Verified by an automated test asserting call ordering.
2. `/skill:standup` performs `wl sync` before its first `wl next` / `wl list` fetch. Verified by an automated test asserting call ordering.
3. The sync invocation is **lock-aware** (uses `wl sync --if-idle`) and single-flight, so overlapping or concurrent invocations skip rather than block or pile up. Verified by a test asserting the `--if-idle` argument / skip behaviour.
4. A **failed sync is non-fatal**: offline, unborn-HEAD, author-gate, or lock-contention failures log a warning and the skill continues with local data, preserving its existing exit-code semantics. Verified by a test that stubs a failing sync and asserts the skill still proceeds.
5. Both `SKILL.md` files document that `wl sync` runs first, what happens on failure, and how to disable it for offline/deterministic runs (`--no-sync`).
6. A `--no-sync` escape hatch (or equivalent injectable runner) exists so tests and offline runs never perform a real network sync; the existing test suites remain hermetic.
7. When no `.worklog` context is resolvable, sync is skipped gracefully rather than erroring.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Target repository:** the `refactor` and `standup` skills are maintained in the **SorraAgents agent-framework repo** (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/...`). This work item is tracked in the **ContextHub** worklog; see Open Questions — implementation location must be confirmed before the implement workflow can run.
- Sync must be bounded and non-interactive; it must never hang an agent session.
- No new third-party dependencies.
- Reuse the existing `wl` CLI and the shared `run_wl` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`) rather than shelling out ad hoc; a single shared helper should serve both skills to avoid divergence.
- Must not change refactor scan/detection semantics or standup report content/format.
- Respect repo ignore rules and the author-gate behaviour of `wl sync` (do not add `--allow-foreign-author`).

## Existing state

- **No skill currently runs `wl sync`.** A search of `skill/**/scripts/*.py` for sync calls returns none (only the `wl` CLI itself and the ContextHub herdr auto-sync).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` exposes `run_wl(cmd)`, which injects `--worklog-dir` with prefix/cwd resolution — the natural wrapper for a shared `sync_worklog()` helper.
- `wl sync` supports `--if-idle` ("Skip (exit 0) if another sync is already in progress — lock-aware guard for auto-sync spawners"), `--no-push`, `--worklog-dir`, and `--json`.
- ContextHub's `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` already implements the `--if-idle` fire-and-forget pattern (single-flight guard + heartbeat freshness) — a proven precedent for non-blocking, non-fatal sync.
- `refactor.py` entry point: `main()` → `_build_pipeline_runner()` → pipeline; session mode wraps `StatusLifecycle(restore_on_exit=True)`.
- `generate_standup.py` entry point: `main()` resolves `--worklog-dir` then calls `generate_report()` which performs the `wl next` / `wl list` fetches via `fetch_json`.
- Existing tests: `skill/standup/tests/` (3 files: default output path, worklog-dir, regressions). Refactor has no dedicated test package in the skill tree.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py`) that runs `wl sync --if-idle` via `run_wl`, returns success/skip status, and never raises on failure.
2. Invoke it as the first action in both `refactor.py` and `generate_standup.py`, before any other `wl` call.
3. Add `--no-sync` to both scripts and thread it through so tests/offline runs skip syncing.
4. Update both `SKILL.md` files to state sync-first behaviour and the `--no-sync` flag.
5. Add focused tests for ordering, `--if-idle`, failure tolerance, and `--no-sync`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — invoke shared sync-first helper before the pipeline in `main()`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — invoke shared sync-first helper in `main()` before `generate_report()`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — **new** shared helper wrapping `wl sync --if-idle` via `run_wl` (fail-soft).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document sync-first + `--no-sync`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/SKILL.md` — document sync-first + `--no-sync`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_sync_first.py` — **new** ordering / failure / `--no-sync` tests.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/tests/test_refactor_sync_first.py` — **new** ordering / failure / `--no-sync` tests.

## Related work

- **ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`** — existing `wl sync --if-idle` single-flight/heartbeat implementation; reuse its semantics/guard pattern (see WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W heartbeat, WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME dispatch parallelism).
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** — *Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head* — standup's data source/ranking is anchored to the Herdr selection list; sync-first affects the freshness of that input.
- **SA-0MTSNTZOV006P79V** — *Refactor skill should run immediately when invoked without an ID* — established the refactor invocation convention; the sync-first step must fit inside it without adding prompts.
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX / SA-0MSGH57JL001OZER** — recent `wl sync` robustness work (identity gate; no-commit repos) — informs the failure-tolerance AC.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "all worklog-reading skills should sync first" is a tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to `refactor` and `standup`; track a generalisation as a separate work item if desired.
- **Latency/lock-contention risk:** an unconditional blocking sync could stall agent sessions. **Mitigation:** `--if-idle`, bounded/non-interactive invocation, non-fatal on failure.
- **Hermetic-test risk:** real syncs in CI would hit the network/author gate. **Mitigation:** injectable runner + `--no-sync`, asserted in tests.
- **Cross-repo risk:** the code lives in SorraAgents while the work item is in ContextHub; the implement workflow's worktree is repo-scoped. **Mitigation:** producer decision on work-item placement (Open Question 1).
- **Assumption:** "first thing run" means the first *worklog operation* — argument parsing, help, and `--worklog-dir` resolution may precede it.
- **Assumption:** sync failure should not abort the skill (read-only/analysis workflows should still produce output from local data).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION 1 — Repository / worklog ownership.** The `refactor` and `standup` skills live in the **SorraAgents** repo (`SorraAgents/skill/...`), but this item is in the **ContextHub** worklog (WL-). The implement workflow creates a worktree in the work-item's repo and refuses changes outside it, so the target repo must be explicit. **Recommended:** implement in SorraAgents under a linked SA work item (agent-framework is the canonical skills home), with this WL item recording the requirement and cross-referencing it. — Awaiting producer.
- **OPEN QUESTION 2 — Where should the sync run?** (A) In the scripts (`refactor.py`, `generate_standup.py`) as the first executable step; (B) only as prose in `SKILL.md` for the agent to run. **Recommended:** (A) — deterministic and testable — plus documented in `SKILL.md`. — Awaiting producer.
- **OPEN QUESTION 3 — Failure and concurrency semantics.** Should a failed sync abort the skill or warn-and-continue? Should the sync use `--if-idle`? And should a `--no-sync` escape hatch exist for tests/offline? **Recommended:** warn-and-continue, `--if-idle`, and a `--no-sync` flag — Awaiting producer.

## Problem statement

WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME makes the downtime dispatcher pass a mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` to dispatched audit panes: `2` in cheap mode when a second local slot is genuinely free and the dispatch is single-flight, `1` otherwise. The benefit has not been observed yet. The first post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained no dispatched audits, so the audit-only `PARALLELISM=2` path was never exercised.

This item is the operational follow-up: capture a measurement that actually exercises the path.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants to confirm the change raises cheap-window local slot utilisation without increasing remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-change proxy usage report covering at least one 01:00-10:00 cheap window recorded, and a dispatched audit within that window shown to overlap its Phase 2 children with the parent (peak cheap-mode concurrency 2, not 1).
2. Cheap-window local utilisation compared against the immediate pre-change cheap windows and the 2026-08-22_3 reference, and reported (up, flat, or down). Utilisation is measured by **avg concurrency (while busy) = total compute ÷ busy time** and/or **slot utilisation = total compute ÷ (window × slots)**, not by busy % (which saturates at one busy slot).
3. Remote fallback rate compared against the pre-change rate and reported (must not increase).
4. Dispatched-audit Phase 2 wall-clock (per audit, or median across audits) compared against a pre-change sequential (`PARALLELISM=1`) audit and reported.
5. If the benefit is not observed (utilisation flat/down, or fallback up), a follow-up work item is created with the finding and a proposed remedy.

## Measurement method and baselines

- **Metric.** Busy % (union of ≥1-active-slot intervals ÷ duration) is a coverage/guardrail metric only — it cannot distinguish one busy slot from two. Primary metric: **avg concurrency while busy** and **slot utilisation**; plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap. # Interview: LLM-Assisted Question Extraction

**Headline:** When `wl interview <id>` finds no parseable questions using the deterministic parser, optionally invoke a local LLM (via the existing embedding infrastructure) to extract unanswered questions from the description in free text.

## Problem Statement

The deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection` + `parseQAPairs`) requires an exact section header and rigid formatting. Real work items use varied formats (e.g., `## Appendix: Clarifying questions \& answers` with `- **Q1**: "..." — Answer (user@...): "..."). As a result, zero of the 17 `needsProducerReview=true` items are currently detectable. The original audit rejected WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 stating: "The command does not reliably detect questions."

An LLM normaliser turns this hard format dependency into a soft one — it can extract questions regardless of prose format.

## Users

- **Producers** running `wl interview <id>` — they want the command to find questions even when the description doesn't follow the canonical format.
- **Developers** — they want the feature to work with local models (Ollama/Foundry), not require a cloud API key.

**User Story:** "As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they're written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible embedding infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`.
2. The LLM is asked to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
3. Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively (same `createPromptLoop` readline flow) for confirmation and answer.
4. Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the **deterministic re-serialiser** (`rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`) — never written directly from LLM output.
5. When no LLM is available (no config, network failure, timeout), the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error.
6. The LLM call is bounded: description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced.
7. Tests cover: mock client returns valid questions, mock returns empty, mock throws error, no config available, timeout.

## Configuration

Opt-in via one of:
- `--llm` CLI flag: `wl interview <id> --llm`
- Config file: `intelligent: true` under `interview` section in `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Constraints

- No new dependencies — reuse `src/lib/search.ts` embedding infrastructure (OpenAI-compatible client, config resolution, graceful degradation).
- LLM is a *text completion* client, not an embedding client — but the same provider config, base URL, model, and auth apply. We should either:
  - (a) Add a `llm.*` config section parallel to `embedding.*`
  - (b) Or reuse the same provider config (the embedder already supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- The deterministic parser remains the primary path; LLM is strictly a fallback.
- Output is interactive-only (no --json mode for LLM calls).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New `--llm` option, LLM client invocation, user confirmation loop for extracted questions.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `src/lib/search.ts` — Potentially add a `ChatClient` class alongside the existing `OpenAIEmbedder`, or reuse its config resolution for a completion client.
- `src/config.ts` — Add `interview.llm` or `llm.*` config schema.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — New test cases for LLM path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Model availability:** Not all setups have an LLM configured. Fallback must be silent and graceful.
- **Cost:** One completion call per invocation (~2-3 KB input) is cheap even at $0.001/call, but should be bounded.
- **Hallucination:** The mandatory user-confirmation step before writing to the description mitigates this.
- **Scope creep risk:** Users may want batch extraction across multiple items or LLM-generated answers. Track separately.
