# Bug — Stage filters hide in-progress items

## Problem

Stage-filtered worklist views (`/wl plan`, `/wl plan_complete`, `/wl intake`, `/wl intake_complete`) run `fetchItemsByStage()` which issues `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only`. Per **AC2 of WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** (confirmed by operator in the brief's Appendix Q2), the "open" status filter explicitly excludes items with `status=blocked`, `status=in-progress`, or `status=completed`.

Before the `in_progress` stage was retired, this was harmless: actively-worked items sat in `stage=in_progress` and the rule only excluded from other stage lists. After **WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX** ("Remove the in_progress stage"), an actively-worked item retains its pipeline stage (`plan_complete` or `intake_complete`) and only flips `status` to `in-progress`. The exclusion now makes actively-worked items **invisible** in the stage filter that corresponds to their pipeline position.

## Concrete example

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | **WL-0MSZVB902004AZZN** ("Pre-fill vs working in Web UI") |
| stage | `plan_complete` |
| status | `in-progress` |
| assignee | Map |

This item is actively being implemented by the herdr downtime worker (agent "Map"). It is **not visible** when a user filters by `plan`/`plan_complete` in the herdr worklist, even though it belongs in that stage. The user sees 0 items belonging to the item's stage while work is underway.

## Root cause

`fetcher.ts` `STAGE_STATUS` defaults every stage to `status=open` with a single-stage exception for `in_review` (fixed in **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW**). No exception exists for stages where claimed work is possible (`plan_complete`, `intake_complete`).

The dispatcher's safety guarantee (prevent re-dispatch of claimed work) comes from the **CAS claim** (`wl update --status in-progress --if-status ...`), not from UI-level exclusion. The UI exclusion provides protection but at the cost of making actively-worked items invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Filtering by `plan_complete` in the herdr worklist shows all items in that stage, including those with `status=in-progress`.
2. Filtering by `intake_complete` in the herdr worklist shows all items in that stage, including those with `status=in-progress`.
3. The `fetchItemsByStage()` function applies `--status open,in-progress` for stages that can hold claimed work (`plan_complete`, `intake_complete`), and `--status open` only for stages that cannot (`idea`, `completed`, `done`).
4. The existing `in_review` exception (`completed,in-progress,open`) is preserved and verified by tests.
5. A unit test asserts the correct `--status` argument per stage, including `in-progress` for `plan_complete` and `intake_complete`.
6. No regression: items with `status=blocked` or `status=completed` remain excluded from non-review stages.
7. The Pi TUI worklist stage filter follows the same pattern (both CLI and DB paths in `tools.ts`).

## Design decisions considered

1. **Per-stage exception list (preferred)**: `STAGE_STATUS` maps each stage to its allowed status set. This is the same approach used for `in_review` in WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW but applied systematically.
2. **`--status open,in-progress` for all stages except completed/done**: Simpler but would surface items with `status=in-progress` in the `idea` stage (should not happen but protects against data corruption).
3. **Remove status filter from stage filter entirely**: Would show `blocked` and `completed` items too, which is worse UX.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage" (origin of the `status=open` rule)
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** — "Herdr: in_review stage filter shows 0 items" (same failure class, fixed only for `in_review`)
- **WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX** — "Remove the in_progress stage" (created the conditions for this bug)
- **WL-0MSZVB902004AZZN** — "Pre-fill vs working in Web UI" (concrete example of the bug in action)

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `STAGE_STATUS`, `fetchItemsByStage()`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — `createListWorkItemsWithStage`, `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` (must stay in sync)
- Test files: `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` (fetcher tests), TUI extension tests

# Machine-Hygiene Skill — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

A global `machine-hygiene` skill that automates the manual performance-pressure analysis performed on 2026-09-27 (which resolved load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned `audit_runners` and stale vite servers). The skill provides a repeatable, safe diagnostic-and-remediation workflow for hosts running many concurrent pi agent sessions and test suites. It never acts autonomously without explicit producer approval.

**Headline:** Create the `machine-hygiene` global skill with a 6-step diagnostic-and-remediation workflow, configurable thresholds, before/after metric tables, and explicit approval gates before any destructive action.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs an automated, safe way to identify and resolve machine performance pressure without manually inspecting processes.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — can invoke the skill to auto-diagnose machine health during idle periods and report actionable findings.
- **Agents** — benefit from a cleaner, more responsive host machine when running multiple sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Global skill structure.** A skill named `machine-hygiene` exists under `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` with a `SKILL.md`, a `scripts/` directory, and tests per skill-authoring conventions. It is discoverable via `/skill: machine-hygiene`.

2. **AC2 — Diagnostic evaluation (Step 1).** The skill collects and renders a **before table** with the following metrics: load average (vs. core count), `/proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}` (percentages), free memory and swap usage, process and thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS (top 10), runnable process count, and stale device detection (zombie processes, stale files/locks). Each metric is classified as **low** (green), **warning** (amber), or **critical** (red) using configurable thresholds.

3. **AC3 — Pressure analysis (Steps 2–3).** The skill describes the primary pressures — identifying which processes/resources contribute most, their attributable ancestry (parent processes, systemd units, session IDs), and proposes concrete remediation actions (kill, renice, prune stale sessions, pace concurrent work), each with target PIDs/paths and expected impact.

4. **AC4 — Approval gate (Step 4).** The skill **stops** and presents findings to the operator/producer, awaiting explicit approval. No destructive action (kill, delete, modify) is taken before approval.

5. **AC5 — Conditional action (Step 5).** Only the explicitly approved subset of proposed actions is executed. The skill tracks which actions were approved vs. declined and reports accordingly.

6. **AC6 — After table (Step 6).** An **after table** is rendered alongside the before table showing current state for each metric, with per-metric priority annotations, and reports residual/legitimate load (e.g., active test suites, ongoing sessions).

7. **AC7 — Threshold configuration.** Low/warning/critical thresholds are configurable via a YAML config file (`~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml`) with documented sensible defaults. Defaults cover: CPU pressure (>70% warning, >85% critical), memory usage (>80% warning, >95% critical), I/O pressure (>50% warning, >80% critical), load average (>cores*0.7 warning, >cores*1.5 critical), zombie processes (>5 warning, >20 critical).

8. **AC8 — Tests.** Tests cover: threshold classification logic, the approval-gate refusal path (verify no destructive action without approval), metric collection on synthetic/fixture data, and config-file override behavior.

9. **AC9 — Documentation.** The skill is documented in `SKILL.md` with invocation examples, and is discoverable via `/skill: machine-hygiene`.

10. **AC10 — Full suite and documentation freshness.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, `SKILL.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries), and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only by default.** Destructive actions (kill, delete, modify) are gated behind explicit operator/producer approval.
- **No direct .worklog mutation.** Any work-item side effects must use `wl` commands.
- **Reusable across projects.** Global skill under `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/`, with tests per skill-authoring conventions.
- **Process management scope only.** The skill focuses on process management (kill, renice, prune, pace). Resource-limiting via cgroups/systemd is out of scope.
- **Configurable thresholds.** Thresholds are configurable via YAML with sensible defaults.

## Existing State

- Manual machine-health analysis was performed on 2026-09-27, resolving load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned `audit_runners`, and stale vite servers.
- Related root causes are documented in:
  - `WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F` — debug-log rotation (audit debug log hygiene)
  - `WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS` — session close lifecycle (orphaned sessions, abandoned panes)
- Existing skills provide patterns: `cleanup` (branch pruning), `context-audit` (context measurement), and `heartbeat` (automated work monitoring).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — **new**: skill entry point with the 6-step workflow and approval gate
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/evaluate.py` — **new**: main entry point; orchestrates Steps 1–6
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py` — **new**: collects and classifies performance metrics (load, pressure, memory, swap, procs, RSS)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — **new**: analyses primary pressures, identifies root causes, proposes remediation actions
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/actions.py` — **new**: executes approved remediation actions (kill, renice, prune)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/tables.py` — **new**: renders before/after tables with status symbols
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — **new**: configurable thresholds with documented defaults
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — **new**: threshold classification and metric collection tests
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — **new**: pressure analysis and remediation proposal tests
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_approval_gate.py` — **new**: approval-gate refusal tests

## Related Work

- `WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F` — Audit debug log retention (related: log-related resource consumption)
- `WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS` — Session close lifecycle (related: orphaned sessions, abandoned panes contributing to pressure)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/cleanup` — Branch cleanup skill (pattern reference for skill structure)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit` — Context measurement skill (pattern reference for metric collection)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/heartbeat` — Automated work monitoring (pattern reference for scheduled analysis)

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The skill runs on Linux with access to `/proc/pressure/` and standard process inspection tools (`ps`, `top`). Non-Linux platforms may need adaptation (documented as a follow-up).
- **Risk — false positives on RSS aggregation.** Per-command RSS grouping can be noisy when many instances of the same binary run under different names. Mitigation: group by process name (not command line) and show top 10 with individual PID breakdowns.
- **Risk — killing the wrong process.** Kill actions must include process ancestry verification (parent, session, uid) before execution. The approval gate requires operator confirmation for each kill.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Resource-limiting (cgroups, systemd) and I/O throttling are tempting but would significantly expand scope. Explicitly out of scope.
- **Risk — stale device detection accuracy.** Zombie processes and stale locks can be legitimate (e.g., during test teardown). The skill should flag rather than auto-remediate these; flagged items are always presented for approval, never auto-executed.
- **Scope-creep opportunity:** A scheduled cron-based auto-hygiene mode (runs at intervals, logs to a file) — captured as a linked follow-up, not in scope. This could be a separate `WL` child item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Skill name and location.** Should the skill be called `host-hygiene`, `perf-hygiene`, or `machine-hygiene`, and should it be global or project-scoped? **Answer (producer):** Proceed with `machine-hygiene` as a global skill under `~/.pi/agent/skills/`. **Final: `machine-hygiene`, global.**
- **Q2 — Threshold configuration.** Should thresholds be hardcoded, configurable, or both? **Answer (producer):** Proceed with configurable via YAML with sensible defaults. **Final: YAML config with documented defaults.**
- **Q3 — Action types beyond kill/prune.** Should the skill recommend resource-management actions like `nice`/`renice` or cgroup limits? **Answer (producer):** Focus on process management (kill, renice, prune, pace). cgroup/systemd resource-limiting is out of scope. **Final: process management only.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD** – Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (completed)
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W** – Recovery: classify 'All providers unavailable ... time window' 503 as SERVER_ERROR (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mujl1nah0042gos, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+238 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: action, actionable, active, agent, agents (+194 more)

# CLI: treat `--parent null` as detach instead of creating a bogus `WL-NULL` parent

**As a** CLI/TUI user managing work-item hierarchy, **I want** `--parent null` to detach an item (set `parentId` to `null`), **so that** detaching a work item is discoverable and does not silently corrupt the hierarchy with an invalid parent reference.

## Problem

`normalizeCliId()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) turns any bare token into `<PREFIX>-<TOKEN>`:

```ts
if (trimmed.includes('-')) return trimmed.toUpperCase();
return `${prefix}-${trimmed.toUpperCase()}`;
```

So `wl update <id> --parent null` produces the literal parent id **`WL-NULL`**, which does not exist. The item ends up with a dangling parent link rather than becoming top-level. The only working detach syntax today is the undocumented `--parent ""`.

### Evidence

- Reproduced live during the v1.0.16 release follow-up: `wl update WL-0MTF5WNZV003JKMJ --parent null` set `parentId = "WL-NULL"` (fixed with `--parent ""`).
- Two pre-existing items still carry the artefact: **WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA** and **WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R** (both `done`, `parentId = "WL-NULL"`).
- `wl show WL-NULL` → "Work item not found".

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl update <id> --parent null` (case-insensitive) detaches the item: `parentId` becomes `null`, exit code 0, no `WL-NULL` written.
2. The same sentinel is accepted by `wl create` (`--parent null` == top-level item, the default).

5. `--parent` help text documents the detach form; `CLI.md` and `EXAMPLES.md` document it.
6. `wl doctor` detects dangling `WL-NULL` (or any non-existent) parent references and proposes a fix; the two known items are remediated.

## Suggested implementation

- Add a small `normalizeParentId(value, prefix)` helper (in `src/cli-utils.ts`) that maps case-insensitive `null` / `none` / `nil` / `-` (and empty string) to `null`, otherwise delegates to `normalizeCliId()`.
- Use it at both call sites: `src/commands/update.ts` (`parentCandidate`, ~L163) and `src/commands/create.ts` (`parentId`, ~L198).
- Keep `normalizeCliId()` unchanged so other id fields are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl update <id> --parent null --json` sets `parentId: null`; `wl show <id> --json` confirms; no item is created or referenced as `WL-NULL`.
2. `wl create --title "x" --parent null --json` creates a top-level item (`parentId: null`).
3. `wl update <id> --parent ""` and `--parent none` both detach (documented aliases).
4. `wl update <id> --parent WL-DOESNOTEXIST` still errors (unchanged).
5. Unit tests for the new helper cover `null`, `NULL`, `none`, `-`, `""`, and a real/partial id.
6. CLI integration tests cover update-detach and create-top-level via `--parent null`.
7. `--parent` help text and `CLI.md`/`EXAMPLES.md` document detach.
8. `wl doctor` flags existing `WL-NULL` parent references; WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA and WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R are cleaned to `parentId: null`.
9. `npm run build` and the full suite pass (build → test → commit order).

## Key files

- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `normalizeCliId`; add `normalizeParentId`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L163)
- `src/commands/create.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L198)
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — dangling-parent check
- `tests/unit/cli-args.test.ts` (or equivalent) — helper unit tests
- `tests/cli/` — update/create integration tests
- `CLI.md`, `EXAMPLES.md`

## Notes

- `--parent null` for `wl list` / `wl search` (filter for root items) is a separate semantics question and is out of scope here.

# Pane-Triage Skill: Approval-Gated Idle Pane Cleanup

## Problem Statement

Agents that end with `</end_session>` leave their herdr pane open, causing idle panes to accumulate and hold memory/CPU. The automatic reaper (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3) handles unattended closure, but producers need a manual, workspace-scoped, approval-gated companion to review and close idle panes — particularly for panes with pending producer review or other special cases.

## Users

**Producer** — Runs several herdr workspaces with active agents. Wants to:
- *As a producer, I want `/skill:pane-triage` to scan my current workspace and report idle vs active panes, with work-item context and producer-review status, so I can decide which panes to close.*
- *As a producer, I want the skill to show a log tail for each idle pane, so I can verify completion before approving closure.*
- *As a producer, I want to explicitly approve or select which panes to close, so I retain full control.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:pane-triage` resolves the invoking workspace from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback `herdr pane current`) and reports only that workspace.
2. Idle classification uses the **shared classifier** (`classifySession` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`) — the last non-empty session entry must be an assistant message ending with `</end_session>` (`.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')`).
3. The report renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle items, the work item id (parsed from pane label) and `needsProducerReview` value.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. A "Recommended to close" table lists idle panes and excludes the invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and panes with `needsProducerReview=true`; the never-close guard applies universally (manual and automatic).
6. No pane is closed without explicit producer approval (`yes`/`select`); `no`/ambiguity closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
7. Approved panes are **re-verified** idle immediately before closing via re-read of `herdr pane list`; any pane that became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.
8. Offline fixture tests cover classification (via shared classifier), marker-mid-message rejection, work-item id parsing, `needsProducerReview` mapping, recommendation rules, and approval gating (no approval → zero close calls).

## Constraints

- **Shared classifier is mandatory** — do NOT reimplement idle state logic. Import `classifySession` and `extractFinalAssistantText` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`.
- **Shared reaper deps for closure** — import `createHerdrReaperDeps` and `runReaper` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` for pane enumeration and closure.
- **Never-close guards** (from classifier, universal): `implement` panes, items with `needsProducerReview=true`, the invoking pane, and panes with live child processes are never closed — **by both the automatic reaper and the manual skill** (producer confirmed).
- **Approval gate is mandatory** — this is the manual complement to the automatic reaper; it never closes anything unattended.
- **Workspace-scoped only** — no cross-workspace roll-up.
- **Skill placement**: Global skill at `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` (symlinked via `~/.pi/agent/skills/`). Tracked in ContextHub.

## Existing State

- **Shared classifier** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `classifySession()`, `extractFinalAssistantText()`, `DEFAULT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`, `SessionSample` type, `CloseDecision` type.
- **Reaper orchestration** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `runReaper(deps, options)`, `ReaperDeps` interface with `listPanes()`, `closePane(paneId)`, `terminateProcessGroup(pid)`.
- **Production wiring** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `createHerdrReaperDeps(io)`, `parseHerdrPaneCloseList()`, `paneKindFromLabel()`, `paneItemIdFromLabel()`, `readFinalAssistantEntries()`.
- **Dependency**: `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM → WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` (completed, in_review).

## Desired Change

A new global skill `/skill:pane-triage` that:
1. Enumerates tabs and panes in the current workspace
2. Classifies each pane using the shared classifier
3. Enriches idle panes with work-item context and producer-review status
4. Displays a structured markdown report
5. Prompts for approval before closing
6. Re-verifies panes immediately before closing
7. Logs closure results in a per-pane ledger

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — Skill specification (what the agent reads)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane-triage.py` — Main skill script (invoked by agent)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` — Python module with core logic:
  - `resolve_workspace()` — get workspace ID from env or `herdr pane current`
  - `enumerate_panes(workspace_id)` — call `herdr tab list` + `herdr pane list`
  - `classify_panes(panes)` — use shared classifier via `createHerdrReaperDeps`
  - `build_report(idle_panes, active_panes, invoking_pane_id)` — markdown output
  - `prompt_approval(recommended_panes)` — blocking prompt: yes/select/no
  - `close_panes(pane_ids)` — re-verify and close, one at a time
  - `parse_workspace_id()` — extract from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`
  - `get_needs_producer_review(item_id)` — call `wl show --json` to check
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/tests/test_pane_triage.py` — Offline fixture tests

## Related Work

- **WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3** — Implement closure reaper script (shared classifier, reaper orchestration, production wiring) — **COMPLETED**, dependency satisfied.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — Log all dispatches and auto-close all completed dispatch panes (dispatch monitor) — completed.
- **WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN** — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception — completed.
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion — evaluated for deferral to this skill.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should this skill live in the global skills directory or ContextHub-local? — A: **Global** at `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` (tracked in ContextHub), so it is available to all agents. ContextHub-local would limit availability.
- Q: How should a Python skill consume the TypeScript shared classifier? — A: **Producer (Q-OPEN-1):** Add a `--json` output mode to `runReaperCli` in ContextHub; the Python skill shells out to the compiled CLI. Keeps skill Python-only. Source: producer reply (intake).
- Q: May the manual skill close `needsProducerReview=true` panes after approval? — A: **Producer (Q-OPEN-2):** Never close — the never-close guard applies universally (manual skill + automatic reaper). Source: producer reply (intake).
- Q: How should the work-item id be parsed from the pane label? — A: Use the shared `paneItemIdFromLabel()` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — matches trailing ` - <PREFIX>-<HASH>` pattern.
- Q: Should `needsProducerReview` use the shared reaper deps or a direct `wl show` call? — A: Direct `wl show <id> --json` call in the skill script (the shared reaper deps' `getNeedsProducerReview` is for the reaper's injected I/O; the skill can call wl directly).
- Q: What is the exact idle classification check? — A: Use the shared `classifySession()` from `pane-close.ts` — it implements the `.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')` check. The skill must NOT re-implement this logic.
- Q: How should the skill handle herdr CLI errors? — A: Fail-closed: clear error message, no partial mutation. If `herdr pane list` fails, report the error and exit.
- Q: What happens if a pane becomes active during the approval prompt? — A: The re-verify-before-close step (AC7) handles this: re-read `herdr pane list` immediately before closing and drop any pane that is no longer idle.

## Open Questions (needs producer input)

### Q-OPEN-1 — How should a Python skill consume the TypeScript shared classifier?

**Context.** Skills in `SorraAgents/skill/` are Python-only (`~/.pi/agent/skills`
symlinks to `SorraAgents/skill`; no skill currently ships TypeScript/JS). The
mandated shared classifier, `classifySession` / `extractFinalAssistantText`, and
the reaper (`createHerdrReaperDeps` / `runReaper`) live in TypeScript at
`packages/herdr/src/pane-close*.ts` and compile to `packages/herdr/dist/`. There
is no standalone `herdr` CLI triage command and no `bin` entry, so there is no
current cross-language invocation path.

**Why it matters.** The spec says "import `classifySession` ... do not copy its
logic into the skill", but a Python module cannot import TypeScript. The choice
determines file layout, build/test story, and part of the effort estimate.

**Options.**

1. **Thin Node bridge (preferred).** Ship `scripts/pane-triage-bridge.mjs`
   which imports the compiled `dist/pane-close-herdr.js` + `pane-close.js`,
   enumerates panes, and emits a JSON report (classification + session tail) to
   stdout. The Python skill owns rendering, the approval prompt, re-verification
   and the ledger. Reuses the classifier verbatim; adds one non-Python script to
   a skill (unprecedented but small).
2. **Add a `--json` output mode to `runReaperCli`** in ContextHub and have the
   Python skill shell out to the compiled CLI. Keeps skill Python-only, but
   enlarges the shared surface (and the reaper is currently only wired into the
   herdr plugin, not exposed as a standalone binary).
3. **Write the skill in TypeScript/Node** under `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/`.
   Direct imports, but breaks the Python-skill convention and repo tooling.

**Preferred (needs confirmation):** Option 1.

### Q-OPEN-2 — May the manual skill close `needsProducerReview=true` panes after approval?

AC5 / the recommend-to-close rules say idle panes with
`needsProducerReview=true` **are** recommended to close, annotated
`review-pending`; the constraints say such items are "never closed". The
intended reading is that the never-close guard applies to the **unattended**
automatic reaper only, and the manual skill may close review-pending panes after
explicit producer approval. Confirm.

**Producer answer (Q-OPEN-2):** If marked `needsProducerReview`, do **not**
close. The never-close guard applies universally — to both the manual skill
and the automatic reaper. This resolves the AC5/approval conflict: `needsProducerReview=true`
panes are excluded from the "Recommended to close" table entirely.

# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.
4. The banner remains display-only: it never disables downtime dispatch, never
   writes/clears `.herdr-downtime-disabled`, and does not change code-freeze
   banner behaviour or the `showHelpText` gate.
5. Automated tests assert the exact rendered banner text for both variants and
   for the boundaries (deep+outstanding → deep+none; deep → shallow), using the
   existing worklist render test seams.
6. All related documentation/code comments describing the banner are updated to
   the new copy and the outstanding-audit condition.

## Constraints

- **Source repository:** the banner is implemented in the **ContextHub** repo
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), not in `AI_Hell`. This work item is tracked
  in the `AI_Hell` worklog (consistent with existing tooling work items such as
  AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV); implementation must target the ContextHub source tree.
- `browseItemCount` default 20, re-read live from settings (no restart).
- Root-only counting via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` (same query as `fetchCompletedItemCount`).
- No new persistence mechanism; reuse existing fetch helpers where possible.
- Display-only; must not reintroduce the sprint-complete auto-disable
  (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD RCA root cause A).
- Keep the change minimal: banner copy + the state needed to choose it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the banner in the footer branch
  (~3596–3617): `const bannerText = \`Review queue deep${countDisplay} — audits will drain it\`;`
  where `countDisplay` = ` (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review)`.
- `refreshSprintState()` (~4531–4546) calls `fetchCompletedItemCount()`
  (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~684) and sets
  `sprintComplete = count >= liveBrowseCount`. Only a count is retained —
  per-item audit state is not currently available to the banner.
- `fetchCompletedItemCount()` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` and returns the item count. `wl list --json` items expose
  `stage`, `status`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`, `fingerprint`, `updatedAt`
  (but not `currentFingerprint`).
- Audit freshness is centralised: `isAuditFresh(...)` in
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (~306) and the audit-aware bucket predicate
  `inReviewBucket(...)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (~360–389). The
  audit-dispatch tier uses the same predicate.
- There are currently **no automated tests** covering the banner text or
  `refreshSprintState` — this gap must be closed.

## Desired change

- Extend the banner-state refresh (or add a sibling helper) so it knows whether
  any root-level `in_review` item has an outstanding audit, in addition to the
  deep-queue boolean.
- Select the banner copy from that state:
  - outstanding audits → `Review queue deep (<n> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`;
  - none outstanding → `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
- Add regression tests for both variants and the transition boundaries.
- Update the code comments that describe the banner to match the new copy and
  condition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — banner copy selection in the footer render
  branch (~3596–3617); `refreshSprintState` (~4531–4546); render-option plumbing
  for `sprintComplete` / `sprintCompletedCount` (~3359–3396, ~5893–5894).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchCompletedItemCount` (~681–699): extend
  or replace with an outstanding-audit-aware fetch of root `completed/in_review`
  items.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh` (~306) shared freshness
  predicate to reuse.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `inReviewBucket` (~360–389) audit-aware
  predicate (alternative reuse).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for both banner
  variants and boundaries.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD** (ContextHub, done/deleted) — P2: replaced the
  sprint-complete auto-disable with the review policy; introduced the current
  "audits will drain it" banner copy.
- **WL-0MTHSHN5V008R5L0** (ContextHub, completed) — Auto-disable dispatching when
  sprint is complete; original sprint-complete banner ("Sprint Complete, hit S to
  ship").
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** (ContextHub, completed) — Allow `/skill:audit` on
  complete/in_review items without a valid audit; defines the "valid audit"
  (`isAuditFresh`) semantics reused here.
- **WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY** (ContextHub, completed) — Ship It shortcut ('S') with
  typed confirmation dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- **WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W** (ContextHub, blocked/plan_complete) — worklist
  pre-dialog ship gate + freeze-on-confirm integration (Ship Guard interaction).
- **WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9** (ContextHub, completed) — review-queue-depth gate for
  non-critical implement dispatch.
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** (ContextHub, completed) — surface held gate in header
  (recent banner/header area change).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "outstanding audit" scope.** Defined as a **root-level**
  `in_review` item with no `auditedAt` or a non-current audit, matching the
  banner's root-only count. If child `in_review` items should also suppress the
  "Ready to Ship" copy, this must be confirmed (see Appendix).
- **Risk — fingerprint availability.** `wl list --json` does not return
  `currentFingerprint`, so `isAuditFresh` degrades to the 60 s time gate and a
  post-audit comment can falsely look stale, keeping "focus on audits" after
  audits complete. Mitigation: compute current fingerprints as the downtime
  worker/hydrator does, or add a purpose-built query.
- **Risk — misleading "Ready to Ship".** The 'S' ship shortcut is gated by the
  Ship Guard (live agent panes carrying this project's work-item IDs block
  shipping). "Ready to Ship" reflects audit state only; changing the guard is out
  of scope.
- **Assumption — condition structure preserved.** Only the deep-queue branch's
  copy changes; the banner still shows only when `isSprintComplete &&
  helpEnabled`.
- **Risk — missing test seams.** There is no existing banner test; the render
  pipeline is internal, so tests must use whatever seam the worklist suite
  already exercises, or expose a small pure helper for the copy decision.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not touch the ship shortcut, Ship Guard, dispatch
  gating, or the queue-depth threshold. Capture extra opportunities as linked
  work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What counts as an "outstanding audit"?**
  — Answer (research; no producer round): the freshness semantics already used
  across herdr — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, fingerprint,
  currentFingerprint)` returning false, or no stored `auditedAt`. Source:
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
  (`inReviewBucket`), and the audit-dispatch tier in `downtime-worker.ts`.
  **ASSUMPTION — root-only scope chosen to match the existing banner count;
  confirm at plan if child `in_review` items should also count.**
- **Q: Where does the banner code live?**
  — Answer (research): the ContextHub repository
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`); this work item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog, consistent with other tooling work items filed there. Source: repo
  search + `wl` config (AI_Hell prefix `AH`, ContextHub prefix `WL`).
- **Q: Is 'S' the ship shortcut?**
  — Answer (research): yes — uppercase 'S' opens the typed-confirmation Ship It
  dialog that dispatches `/skill:ship release` (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY). Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`openShipItDialog`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`) and
  `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
- *Interview style:* no producer interview round was required — the seed
  description plus repo/work-item search sufficed. The only open point is the
  outstanding-audit scope, recorded here as a documented assumption for producer
  confirmation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (completed)
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** – Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats (completed)
- **AH-0MUDY2LRR0040035** – Debris shards and shockwave ring (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: audits, completed, current, currently, depth (+12 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: completed, current, incorrect, like, ready (+7 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: current, currently, deep, depth, focus (+6 more)

---

## Migration provenance

- Re-filed from the AI_Hell work item `AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ` ("Review Queue depth notification is incorrect") on 2026-09-27.
- Reason: the implementation lives in **ContextHub**, but the item was tracked in the AI_Hell worklog. The audit/implement tooling resolves the owning project from the worklog prefix, so a cross-repo item cannot be audited correctly (the audit runner aborts when launched from ContextHub and mis-scopes to AI_Hell when launched from AI_Hell). # Problem Statement

When using the developer cheat menu (Market Card Cheat) to replace a card in the market slot, the replacement card cannot be taken — the HUD shows "No affordable cards" and the card is not interactive.

# Users

- **Developer testers**: The cheat menu is a development/debugging tool used by the development team to test game scenarios quickly.

**User story**: As a developer tester, I want to add any card to the market via the cheat menu and immediately be able to take/buy that card, so that I can test game scenarios without being blocked by the card being unresponsive.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cheat-placed cards are clickable**: After using the Market Card Cheat menu to replace a market slot with a card, clicking the card successfully moves it to the player's hand (no unresponsive card).
2. **Cheat card appears in affordability summary**: The card appears in the "Can buy:" HUD summary (e.g., "Can buy: 1 business") alongside other affordable cards of the same family.
3. **All card families work**: The fix works for all card families supported by the cheat menu (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
4. **Existing cheat functionality preserved**: Filtering, searching, and replacing market cards continue to work as before.

# Constraints

- The fix must be surgical — only modify the `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`.
- Cheat-generated cards already have unique IDs (`${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`) and reset properties (level, incomeBonus, etc.) — `family` should follow the same explicit-set pattern.
- The fix must not affect production gameplay — the cheat menu is strictly a dev/debug tool.

# Existing state

- **Card templates** in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` are typed as `Omit<BusinessCard, 'family' | 'level' | 'incomeBonus' | 'synergyRangeBonus' | 'reputationBonus'>[]` — the `family` field is intentionally **omitted** from templates (it is inferred from the array source).
- **`cheatReplaceMarketCard`** in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` creates cheat cards by spreading the template:
  ```typescript
  const newCard: AnyCard = { ...(template as any), id: `${baseId}--cheat-${cheatNonce++}` } as AnyCard;
  ```
  The function explicitly resets `level`, `incomeBonus`, etc. for business/community-space cards, but **does not explicitly set `family`** — leaving it as `undefined`.
- **Market rendering** in `MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` determines click handlers by checking `card.family`:
  ```typescript
  if (card.family === 'business' || card.family === 'community-space') {
      s.onBusinessCardClick(card as BusinessCard);
  } else if (card.family === 'upgrade') { ... }
  ```
  When `card.family` is `undefined`, none of these conditions match, so the cheat card is not interactive.
- **Affordability check** in `MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` also filters by family:
  ```typescript
  c => (c.family === 'business' || c.family === 'community-space') && c.cost <= state.resourceBank.coins
  ```
  The `undefined` family fails this check, so the card is not shown as "affordable".

# Desired change

Explicitly set the `family` property on cheat-created cards to match the card's actual family, so that rendering and affordability checks work correctly.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function, where the new card is created (fix location)
- `src/MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` — `getAffordableBusinessCards`, `getAffordableUpgradeCards` (affordability checks that depend on `family`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — `refreshMarket` (rendering that routes click handlers by `family`)
- `src/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` — `MarketCardCheatOverlay` (invokes the cheat function, already passes correct `family`)

# Related work

- **WL-0MUH5HU580064VMR** — "Show which cards are in the current deck in the market cards cheat" (related cheat menu feature, separate work item)

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption**: The root cause is the missing `family` field. Verified by code analysis — templates omit `family` and the cheat spread does not set it.
- **Risk**: Minimal scope creep — the fix is a single property assignment in the cheat function.
- **Risk**: If other card properties are also missing from cheat cards (beyond what is already explicitly reset), they may surface later during testing.
- **Risk**: None — no production gameplay impact (cheat menu is dev-only).

# Polish & Handoff

**Headline**: Cheat menu market replacements create cards without a `family` field, making them unclickable and invisible to affordability checks. Fix: explicitly set `family` in `cheatReplaceMarketCard`.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions needed — the root cause was identified through code analysis. The bug is reproducible from the described steps:

1. Open settings → open market card cheat menu
2. Select any card type (e.g., "Pawn Shop")
3. Replace a market slot
4. Close settings
5. The replaced card is not clickable and the HUD shows "No affordable cards"

## Goal

As a herdr operator, I want a minimum cooldown between successive downtime
dispatches of the same work item after a pane ends **without reaching a
terminal stage**, so a repeatedly failing session cannot be re-selected
immediately and waste local-LLM slots.

## Problem Statement

During the 3-hour window examined on 2026-09-28 (05:02–08:02 local), the
downtime dispatcher recorded 6 non-scheduled dispatches. 5 of the
corresponding panes closed with a non-terminal reason code
(`agent-ended-no-terminal` x4, `audit-ended-no-result` x1):

| Item | Kind | Close reason |
|------|------|--------------|
| `WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K` | plan | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG` | intake | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2` | intake | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUH765F1003FKRK` | intake | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUKH3DVA00488U0` | audit | `audit-ended-no-result` |

Re-eligibility of an item after such a close is currently governed only by
the dispatched success-marker TTL (`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`,
24 h) and the stage-advancement guard. There is **no explicit minimum-dwell
cooldown** keyed on the outcome of the previous dispatch, so the policy for
"how soon may we try this item again after it failed" is implicit and
depends entirely on the coarse 24 h marker window. A shorter, deliberate
cooldown is needed so a failed session does not immediately consume another
slot when the marker window is shortened, reset, or bypassed (e.g. critical
escalation, marker-loss, or a stage transition caused by a partial run).

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** runs the downtime dispatcher and expects failed
  sessions not to be retried in a tight loop.
- **Pi agent (AI):** receives auto-dispatches; should not receive the same
  item again until the cooldown elapses.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Cooldown on non-terminal close:** When a downtime pane for an
   item closes with a non-terminal reason code (`agent-ended-no-terminal`,
   `audit-ended-no-result`, or any future non-terminal code), that item is
   excluded from re-dispatch of the **same kind** until at least
   `cooldownMs` has elapsed since the close timestamp.
2. **AC2 — Configurable + clamped:** The cooldown is read from settings
   (`downtimeNonTerminalCooldownMs` or equivalent), re-read fresh each tick,
   with a defensive floor (no immediate retry) and a ceiling (cannot strand
   an item indefinitely). Document the defaults and clamps.
3. **AC3 — Neutral, never a strike:** The cooldown is a neutral skip (like
   `code-freeze` / `audit-in-flight`) — it must NOT count towards the
   three-strike CLI-error rule and must NOT trigger the no-candidate
   cooldown when it is the only reason a candidate was skipped; the terminal
   reason must be distinguishable from `no-candidate`.
4. **AC4 — Stage advancement releases:** If the item advances past its
   dispatched-at stage, the cooldown is released immediately (a genuinely
   progressed item is not held back).
5. **AC5 — Terminal success unaffected:** A successful terminal close
   (e.g. `closed-as-intake-complete`, `closed-as-plan-complete`,
   `reached-in-review`) does not apply the non-terminal cooldown.
6. **AC6 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: (a) non-terminal close then immediate
   idle cycle → skipped with the cooldown reason; (b) close older than
   `cooldownMs` → eligible; (c) stage advancement mid-cooldown → eligible;
   (d) terminal success → eligible per existing semantics; (e) missing /
   unparseable close timestamp → fail-closed skip.
7. **AC7 — Both dispatch paths:** The control applies to BOTH the
   Herdr-list-head path (`dispatchFromHerdrList`) and the coordination
   offer path (`dispatchFromCoordination` / `computeMostImportantItem`).

## Constraints

- TypeScript under `packages/herdr/src/`; reuse the existing rolling dispatch
  log (`downtime-log.ts`) as the source of pane-close outcomes.
- Fail-closed default: if the close outcome cannot be read, prefer the safe
  (no-dispatch) behaviour.
- No second ranking implementation on the dispatch path — this is a
  sequential **filter**, matching the existing gate pipeline.

## Existing State

- Dispatched-marker readers already in `downtime-log.ts`
  (`dispatchedItemMarkers`, `markerStillExcludes`).
- Pane-lifecycle close entries already carry `reasonCode`
  (`pane-lifecycle.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`).
- Gate pipeline documented in `downtime-worker.ts` module header.

## Related Work

- WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2 — discovered-from parent

- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — Herdr audit tier: re-check for a fresh audit after selection, before claim/comment/spawn (completed)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — worker implementation with gate pipeline docs

# Enforce a per-item dispatch-attempt cap and flag items that exhaust it

**Work Item:** `WL-0MUKYEXMK0033MFK`

---

## Problem Statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher has no per-item attempt budget. Re-dispatch is bounded only by the success-marker TTL and the stage-advancement guard. Repeated non-terminal closes (observed as `agent-ended-no-terminal` / `audit-ended-no-result` during the 2026-09-28 review window) can therefore consume local-LLM slots across many idle cycles without any escalation. There is no machine-readable count of how many times the dispatcher has attempted an item, and no threshold at which the item is flagged for producer review.

**Concrete example:** During the 2026-09-28 review window, AI_Hell re-dispatched AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP for `implement` 3× in ~1h45m with the stage unchanged and a live pane still active — a per-item attempt cap would have stopped the loop and flagged the item for producer review.

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** Wants failing items to stop consuming dispatch slots and to be visible for manual triage.
- **Producer/reviewer:** Wants a flag on items that have exhausted their automatic dispatch budget, so they can triage and intervene.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a** Herdr operator, **I want** the downtime dispatcher to stop auto-dispatching an item once it has exceeded a configurable number of attempts for a given skill/kind, **so that** I can reclaim wasted compute and focus on items that are progressing.
- **As a** Producer/reviewer, **I want** items that exhaust their dispatch budget to be automatically flagged (`needsProducerReview = true`) with a clear reason, **so that** I can triage and decide whether to advance the stage, reassign, or close the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Attempt counter:** The dispatcher derives, from the rolling dispatch log, the per-item, per-kind count of dispatch attempts, including attempts whose pane closed non-terminally. No new persistent store is required if the existing log suffices; if a dedicated counter is needed, it must be fail-open (default 0).
2. **AC2 — Cap enforced:** Once the count reaches `maxAttempts` (configurable, clamped to a sane range, default documented), the item is excluded from further automatic dispatch of that kind.
3. **AC3 — Escalation:** On reaching the cap, the item is flagged `needsProducerReview = true` (with a distinct skip reason `attempt-budget-exhausted`) so it surfaces for human triage.
4. **AC4 — Stage advancement resets:** A stage advancement clears the budget for the previous kind (the item has demonstrably progressed and deserves a fresh attempt budget).
5. **AC5 — Neutral skip reason:** A budget-exhausted skip is a neutral reason, distinct from `no-candidate`, and never counts as a CLI-error strike.
6. **AC6 — Both dispatch paths:** The cap applies to BOTH the Herdr-list-head path and the coordination offer path.
7. **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover:
   - (a) count below cap → eligible for dispatch
   - (b) count at cap → skipped with `attempt-budget-exhausted` reason
   - (c) flag set exactly once
   - (d) stage advancement resets the count
   - (e) corrupt/missing log → fail-open count of 0 (never block all dispatch)

## Constraints

- **Language:** TypeScript under `packages/herdr/src/`.
- **Non-breaking:** Must not weaken the existing duplicate-dispatch protections (`WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4`, `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT`) — additive only.
- **Design:** The cap is a sequential **filter** on the ranked candidate sequence, not a new ranking algorithm.
- **Config:** `maxAttempts` should be configurable with a documented default (recommended: 3).

## Existing State

- Rolling dispatch log and marker readers in `downtime-log.ts`.
- `needsProducerReview` is already honoured as a global exclusion by the dispatcher, so setting it is sufficient to stop re-dispatch once flagged.
- The dispatcher uses two paths: (1) normal Herdr-head scan, and (2) coordination offer path — both need the cap applied.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Rolling dispatch log reading; may need a `countAttempts(itemId, kind)` helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatcher selection logic; needs cap enforcement as a filter on both dispatch paths.
- `packages/herdr/src/config.ts` or equivalent — `maxAttempts` configuration (or use existing config mechanism).

## Related Work

- **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement items (completed) — duplicate-dispatch prevention for same worktree.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed) — prior audit/plan-tier RCA.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed).
- **WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2** — Source work item from which this was discovered (3h dispatch-log evaluation).

## Risks & Assumptions

**Risks:**
- Counting from the rolling log is O(n) per item. *Mitigation:* For typical worklog sizes (hundreds to low thousands of entries), this is negligible; add a memoized cache if performance becomes an issue.
- The cap could block genuinely important items that legitimately need retries. *Mitigation:* Stage advancement resets the budget (AC4), and the cap is per-kind so a stage change opens a fresh budget.
- Config changes could accidentally raise the cap too high. *Mitigation:* Clamp to a sane range (e.g., min 1, max 10) with a documented default.

**Assumptions:**
- The rolling dispatch log at `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` contains entries for all dispatch attempts (both successful and non-terminal).
- The `needsProducerReview` flag, once set, is sufficient to exclude the item from dispatcher candidates.
- `maxAttempts = 3` is a reasonable default (based on observed patterns: 2-4 non-terminal retries before human intervention is warranted).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

1. **Q:** What should the default `maxAttempts` value be? — **Answer (agent recommendation):** 3, based on the observed pattern where items exceeding 3 non-terminal retries were unlikely to self-resolve. *Rationale:* Low enough to prevent wasted compute, high enough to allow legitimate retries for transient issues.
2. **Q:** Should the attempt counter be per-kind (per skill) or global per item? — **Answer (agent recommendation, per description):** Per-kind (per skill), as stated in the goal. This allows an item to progress through different skills without the budget for one skill being consumed by retries in another.
3. **Q:** Should the budget reset on ANY stage advancement, or only certain stage transitions? — **Answer (agent recommendation, per description):** On ANY stage advancement, since any advancement demonstrates the item has progressed and deserves a fresh budget for its next kind.

## Headline

The recovery-extension crash fixed for `_notifyFn` (WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B) may be
one of several retained-`ctx` async paths. Audit the recovery module (and
adjacent Worklog extension code) for other captured/stored `ExtensionContext`
references that are invoked asynchronously after a session replacement/reload,
and harden them with the same defensively-guarded pattern.

## Context / Discovered from

- **Discovered from:** WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B (stale-ctx `_notifyFn` crash). The

## Goal (user story)

**As a pi extension maintainer**, I want every asynchronous path in the Worklog
recovery extension that can outlive its original `ExtensionContext` to degrade
gracefully (skip the operation) rather than throw an uncaught exception, so
that a session replacement/reload cannot crash a headless pi run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written audit enumerates every module-level or long-lived reference to a
  handler `ctx` (or a closure capturing it) in
  `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/` and classifies each as either **safe**

After printing the explanation in the `noSection`/`noQuestions` flagged case, interactively ask the user whether to clear `needsProducerReview`.

## Goal

Create a pure filter function that checks whether a non-terminal cooldown
applies to an item+kind pair, based on the rolling pane-close log.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Function `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` in `downtime-log.ts`:
   - Reads `entryType: "pane-close"` entries from the passed entries array
   - Non-terminal reason codes: anything except `"none"` (e.g. `agent-ended-no-terminal`, `audit-ended-no-result`, `producer-review`, `risk-effort-incomplete`, `reached-in-review`)
   - Terminal outcomes have `reasonCode: "none"` - they do NOT trigger cooldown
   - Returns true when: a non-terminal close for the same itemId+kind exists AND cooldownMs has NOT elapsed since the close timestamp
   - Returns false when: no close record, or the close is older than cooldownMs, or the close was terminal
   - Fail-closed: missing/unparseable timestamp returns true (skip dispatch)

2. Stage advancement releases (AC4 of parent):
   - The function receives itemStage (current worklog stage of the item)
   - If the current stage rank is HIGHER than the dispatched-at stage rank, return false (released)
   - Stage rank ordering: idea=0, intake_complete=1, plan_complete=2, in_review=3

3. Tests: Unit tests covering:
   - (a) non-terminal close then immediate idle returns true (skip)
   - (b) close older than cooldownMs returns false (eligible)
   - (c) stage advancement mid-cooldown returns false (eligible)
   - (d) terminal success reasonCode equals none returns false (eligible)
   - (e) missing/unparseable close timestamp returns true (fail-closed skip)

## Feature 3: Implement core pane-triage logic (enumerate, classify, report)

### Summary
Implement the core Python module: workspace resolution, pane enumeration via shelling out to the reaper CLI `--json` mode, report rendering (Idle/Active tables, log tails, recommendation rules), and the approval-gated close flow.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `resolve_workspace()` returns the workspace from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` or falls back to `herdr pane current`; reports only that workspace.
2. `enumerate_and_classify()` shells out to the reaper CLI (`--json`), parses the JSON output, and enriches each pane with work-item context. The item id is derived from the shared `paneItemIdFromLabel` (exposed in the reaper JSON), not re-parsed in Python. The `needsProducerReview` value is obtained via `wl show <id> --json` for the parsed item id.
3. `build_report()` renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle items, the work item id and `needsProducerReview` value. **Idle** specifically means the shared classifier's reasonCode is `'marker'` (the `</end_session>` marker is present at the end of the final assistant message), per parent AC2.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. Recommendation rules: the "Recommended to close" table excludes the invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and panes with `needsProducerReview=true`. Additionally, panes with reasonCode `implement` or `live-children` (inherited from the shared classifier's never-close guards) are also excluded.
6. Re-verify-before-close: re-reads `herdr pane list` immediately before each close; any pane that became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.

### Constraints
- Shared classifier is mandatory: consume idle classification from the ContextHub reaper CLI (`--json`), never re-implement the `</end_session>` check.
- Never-close guards are universal (per producer Q-OPEN-2): `needsProducerReview=true` panes are never closed, by manual skill or automatic reaper. `implement` panes and panes with live child processes are also excluded (inherited from the shared classifier).
- Workspace-scoped only — no cross-workspace roll-up.
- Fail-closed on herdr CLI errors: clear message, no partial mutation.

### Deliverables
- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` (full implementation)
- Updated `SKILL.md` documenting report shape and rules

# Improve Mechanism A idle timeout algorithm and re-enable auto-close

## Problem statement

Mechanism A (the scheduled reaper, `pane-close.ts::classifySession`) has two
classification bugs and should be re-enabled once they are fixed:

1. `!agentProcessAlive` (step 6) currently closes the pane (`dead-agent`).
   A dead agent does not mean the pane is safe to close — the operator may
   still need to read the final output. This should be **no close**.
2. The idle timeout (step 7) only supports a positive threshold. It should
   accept `<= 0` meaning **never close on idle**, with a **default of `0`**
   (idle-based closing disabled by default).

With the idle default at `0`, the auto-close feature can be safely re-enabled
via `paneCloseEnabled` (currently `false`).

## Background

- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — created the pane-lifecycle classifier.
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper.

# Reconsider and disable Mechanism B (dispatch-monitor) pane auto-close

## Problem statement

Mechanism B (`packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts::classifyPaneLifecycle`),
driven from the downtime worker's dispatch monitor, is not working well and is
being **disabled** while the scheduled reaper (Mechanism A) is re-enabled.
Mechanism B needs to be revisited and either fixed or replaced.

## Background

- **WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC** — parent improvement item for pane auto-close.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — created the pane-lifecycle classifier (Mechanism B).
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper
  (Mechanism A).
- **WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI** — fixes Mechanism A and re-enables it.

There are two independent classifiers today:

- **Mechanism A** — `pane-close.ts::classifySession`, run by the scheduled
  reaper. Session-state based (marker / dead agent / idle) with explicit
  never-close guards.
- **Mechanism B** — `pane-lifecycle.ts::classifyPaneLifecycle`, run from the
  downtime worker against the rolling dispatch log. Worklog-stage based.

Mechanism B has been observed to close panes prematurely and to race with
Mechanism A (no shared atomic lock; both check idempotency non-atomically).
With Mechanism A re-enabled and improved, Mechanism B should be switched off
and its design reconsidered rather than left running.

## Current behaviour

- The worker invokes `classifyPaneLifecycle` (see `downtime-worker.ts` around
  the pane-lifecycle pass) and closes panes for every non-`implement` kind,
  including `requires-attention` outcomes.
- Mechanisms A and B use different classifiers and share only a
  non-atomic `alreadyClosedPaneIds` / log-key idempotency set.

## Desired change (this item)

1. Disable Mechanism B's pane-closing behaviour so it does not run.
2. Add an explicit code comment at the Mechanism B call site / module header
   stating that this mechanism is disabled because it is not working well and
   needs to be revisited (with a reference to this work item).
3. Capture the analysis of why Mechanism B misbehaves (stage-propagation lag,
   `requires-attention` still closing, races with Mechanism A) so a future
   session can decide whether to fix, replace, or delete it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — Mechanism B disabled.** The dispatch-monitor pane-close path is
   switched off and does not close panes; Mechanism A remains the only active
   auto-close path.
2. **AC2 — Explicit code comment.** A clear comment in the relevant source
   (module header and/or call site) states that Mechanism B is disabled
   because it is not working well and needs to be revisited, referencing this
   work item.
3. **AC3 — Tests.** Tests assert Mechanism B no longer closes panes (or is not
   invoked) while Mechanism A continues to function; existing Mechanism B unit
   tests are retained but clearly marked as covering disabled behaviour.
4. **AC4 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
5. **AC5 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — Mechanism B classifier (comment / disable)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Mechanism B call site
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.test.ts` — Mechanism B tests

## Related work

- WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic (parent)
- WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI — Improve Mechanism A and re-enable auto-close
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — pane-lifecycle classifier origin
- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — pane-close scheduler/reaper origin

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should happen to Mechanism B?" — Answer (operator): "Leave
  mechanism B disabled and comment in the code to make it clear this is not
  working well and needs to be revisited. Create a work item to reconsider
  this mechanism." Source: interactive reply.
